*$TX$ as an M-polyfold.* For a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, $(TV, T\varphi, (TO, TC, TE))$ is a chart of $TX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartInv⟧; its overlap with another is $T(\varphi(V \cap V'))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_overlap⟧ and its transition map is $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ — formula (5) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_transition⟧ — which is sc-smooth between the tangent retracts by the tangent functor (§II.4); so the charts are compatible ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_compatible⟧, form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentAtlas⟧ and make $TX$ an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold_isChart⟧. *$p : TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth*: in the charts $T\varphi$ and the level chart of $\varphi$ it is the projection $TO \to O_1$, $(a, h) \mapsto a$, which is sc-smooth between the retracts $(TO, TC, TE)$ and $(O_1, C_1, E^1)$ because, with the retraction $Tr$ onto $TO$, $\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ Tr = r_1 \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ on $TU$, a composite of the sc-operator $\mathrm{pr}_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · ScBanach.tangentFst⟧ and the sc-smooth $r_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.isScSmoothRetractMap_tangent_fst⟧; one pair of charts per point suffices (§II.5) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentProj_isScSmooth⟧.

### II.9 The tangent map of an sc-smooth map between M-polyfolds

The text uses $Tf$ for maps between M-polyfolds from §2.3 on without defining it. *The chain rule on chart images, with locality*: for $F$ sc-smooth on $\varphi(s_1)$ into a retract $O_1$ mapping $\varphi(t)$ into $O'_1$, $G$ sc-smooth on $O'_1$ and $H$ sc-smooth on $\varphi(s_2)$ with $H = G \circ F$ on $\varphi(t)$ ($t \subseteq s_1 \cap s_2$ open), $TH = TG \circ TF$ on $T(\varphi(t))$, the three tangent maps computed on their own domains ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MChart.retractTangentMap_comp_image⟧ — Theorem 2.8 on $\varphi(t)$ plus the locality of $Tf$. *Levels*: an sc-smooth map maps $X_m$ into $Y_m$, because its coordinate representations do ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.mapsTo_levelSet⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.mapsTo_levelSet⟧. *The image vector*: for a tuple $(x, \varphi, h)$ and a chart $\psi$ around $f(x)$, $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})(\text{vec})$, computed on $\varphi(V \cap f^{-1}(V'))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.fdom⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport⟧, lies in $TO'$ over $\psi(f(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_fst⟧; changing $\psi$ changes it by $T$ of the transition map ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_transport⟧, changing $\varphi$ by transport ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_eq_of_transport⟧, and equivalent tuples give the same image ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.ftransport⟧ — all by the chain rule with locality. The image tuple $(f(x), \psi, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.fimageWith⟧ therefore has a class independent of $\psi$ and of the representative ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.mk_fimageWith_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.mk_fimageWith_eq_of_rel⟧.

*$Tf$.* With a chosen $\psi$, $Tf[(x, \varphi, h)]$ is the class of the image tuple ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap⟧, computable in any chart around $f(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_mk⟧. It covers $f$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_tangentMap⟧, maps $T_xX$ into $T_{f(x)}Y$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_mapsTo_fiber⟧, and in charts $T\psi \circ Tf = T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ T\varphi$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_tangentMap⟧. $T(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_id⟧, and **the chain rule** $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$ holds: with charts $\psi$ around $f(x)$ and $\chi$ around $g(f(x))$ and the open set $t = \operatorname{fdom}(\varphi, f, \psi) \cap f^{-1}(\operatorname{fdom}(\psi, g, \chi))$, the chain rule with locality gives $T(\chi \circ g \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) = T(\chi \circ g \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $T(\varphi(t))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_comp⟧. $Tf$ is continuous: near a class in $TV$, the preimage of a generating set of $TY$ contains the generating set of $TX$ given by $\varphi$ and the preimage under the continuous $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.continuous_tangentMap⟧; and $Tf$ is sc-smooth $TX \to TY$, its representation in the charts $T\varphi$, $T\psi$ being $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$, sc-smooth by the tangent functor ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_isScSmooth⟧.

### II.10 Sub-M-polyfolds (Definition 2.20, Proposition 2.21)

**Definition 2.20.** $A \subseteq X$ is a *sub-M-polyfold* if every $a \in A$ has an open $V \ni a$ and a map $r$ with $r(V) \subseteq V$, sc-smooth on $V$, idempotent on $V$, with $r(V) = A \cap V$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold⟧; $X$ is one ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_univ⟧. The data at a point are packaged ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold.data⟧: $r$ maps $V$ into $A$, fixes $A \cap V$, and is continuous on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.apply_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.apply_eq_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.continuousOn⟧.

**Proposition 2.21, the structure.** *Shrinking.* For a chart $\varphi$, put $W := (V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi) \cap r^{-1}(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.shrink⟧: open (continuity of $r$) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.isOpen_shrink⟧, containing every $a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.mem_shrink⟧, with $r(W) \subseteq W$ and $r(W) = W \cap A$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.mapsTo_shrink⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.image_shrink⟧. *The retract.* $\rho := \varphi \circ r \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth from $\varphi(W)$ to itself — Definition 2.14 for $r$ in the charts $\varphi$, $\varphi$ — idempotent, and $\rho(\varphi(W)) = \varphi(W \cap A)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_isScSmooth⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_idem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_image⟧; so $\varphi(W \cap A)$ is a retract by Proposition 2.10 (2) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.isScRetract_image⟧. *The chart.* With the subspace topology on $A$, $\varphi$ restricted to $W \cap A$ is a chart of $A$ with model $(\varphi(W \cap A), C, E)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChartInv⟧. *Compatibility.* The overlap of two such charts is $\varphi((W \cap W') \cap A)$, a subset of $\varphi(V \cap V')$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart_overlap⟧. An sc-smooth map between retracts is sc-smooth on every sub-retract $O_1 \subseteq O$: for a retraction $s$ onto $O_1$, $f \circ s = (f \circ r) \circ s$, sc-smooth by the chain rule ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.mono_source⟧ — this is the text's "$(\psi' \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ s'' = (\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ s''$". The transition maps of the sub-charts are restrictions of those of $X$, hence sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart_compatible⟧. They form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subAtlas⟧, and $A$ is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_isChart⟧. The structure requires $A$ to be paracompact (an instance argument); it is, as a subset of the metrizable $X$ (§II.7), and for closed $A$ also elementarily ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_of_isClosed⟧.

*(1) and (2).* The inclusion $A \to X$ is sc-smooth: in the sub-chart and $\varphi$ it is the identity of $\varphi(W \cap A)$ into $O$; one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_inclusion_isScSmooth⟧; it is a homeomorphism onto its image by the choice of topology. For any data $(V, r)$, the map $i^{-1} \circ r$ (a total map with a junk value off $V$) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.retractInto⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.retractInto_val⟧ is sc-smooth on $V$: near $x \in V$ take a chart $\varphi'$ around $x$, a chart $\varphi$ around $r(x)$ and $V_0 = V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi' \cap r^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi)$; on $\varphi'(V_0)$ the representation in $\varphi'$ and the sub-chart on $\varphi$ is $\varphi \circ r \circ \varphi'^{-1}$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.14 for $r$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_retraction_isScSmooth⟧.

**Proposition 2.21 (3), (4), in a chart.** Let $r$ be a retraction onto $O$, $s$ sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to itself with $s \circ s = s$, and $t := s \circ r$, a retraction onto $s(O)$ (Proposition 2.10 (2)) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScRetraction.compRetraction⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScRetraction.compRetraction_retract⟧. For $a \in s(O)_1$ put $P := Dr(a)$, $Q := Dt(a) = D(s \circ r)(a)$ — the text's "$Ds(a)$". Both are idempotent (§II.2). From $r \circ t = t$ and $t \circ r = t$ on $U$ ($s$ takes values in $O$, which $r$ fixes; and $r \circ r = r$), the chain rule at the point $a$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_apply⟧ gives $PQ = Q$ and $QP = Q$. If $a$ is smooth, $P$ and $Q$ are sc-operators (Part I, Proposition 1.16), and so is $P - Q$; identities between base maps of sc-operators hold on every level ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_comp_of_base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_comp_eq_zero_of_base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_eq_add_of_base⟧. Then $Q$ and $P - Q$ are commuting idempotent sc-operators with $Q(P - Q) = 0$, their ranges are sc-subspaces (Part I, §I.3: sc-splittings and sc-projections ⟦Chapter1/ExpositionLemmas · ScBanach.isScSplitting_of_idem⟧), and on every level the level parts of $QE$ and $(P - Q)E$ are disjoint with sum the level part of $PE$. Since $T_aO = PE$ and $T_a s(O) = QE$ (§II.2), this is the sc-splitting $T_aO = T_aA \oplus (Dr(a) - Dt(a))E$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_21_3⟧. For (4), $s$ is sc-smooth from $O$ onto $s(O)$ (shrinking the target), and $Ts(a, h) = (a, Q h)$ for $h \in T_aO$ because $Q h = Q P h$; as $Q$ maps $PE$ onto $QE = Q(PE)$, $Ts(a)$ maps $T_aO$ onto $T_a s(O)$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_21_4⟧. The transport to $T_aX$ is not formalized.

### II.11 The degeneracy index of an M-polyfold (Definitions 2.22, 2.25; Lemmas 2.23, 2.26; Proposition 2.24)

A retract is contained in its quadrant, and chart values lie in $C$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · LocalModel.O_subset_C⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MChart.apply_mem_C⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · LocalModel.isPartialQuadrant⟧. **Definition 2.22.** $d(x, \varphi) := d_C(\varphi(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex⟧, and $d_X(x)$ is the least $d(x, \varphi)$ over the charts of the structure around $x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex⟧; $d_X(x) \le d(x, \varphi)$ for every such chart and the minimum is attained ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex_le⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.exists_isChart_degIndex_eq⟧. **Lemma 2.23.** $d_C$ is upper semicontinuous: coordinates positive at $x$ stay positive nearby, so the vanishing set can only shrink ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · eventually_degIndexWith_le⟧; composed with the continuous chart, $d(\cdot, \varphi)$ is upper semicontinuous on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.eventually_chartDegIndex_le⟧, and with a chart realizing $d_X(x)$, $d_X(y) \le d(y, \varphi) \le d(x, \varphi) = d_X(x)$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · lemma_2_23⟧. Hence $\{d_X < k\}$ is open and $\{d_X \ge k\}$ closed ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isOpen_setOf_degIndex_lt⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_setOf_le_degIndex⟧.

**Proposition 2.24.** An sc-diffeomorphism of open sets is $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, $g$ sc-smooth on $V$, mapping into each other and mutually inverse ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.symm⟧. For a chart $\psi$ of $Y$, $\psi \circ f$ on $U \cap f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)$, with inverse $g \circ \psi^{-1}$, is a chart of $X$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.transportChart⟧; it is compatible with every chart $\varphi$ of the atlas of $X$, because its transition maps with $\varphi$ are $\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi \circ g \circ \psi^{-1}$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.14 for $f$ and for $g$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.transportChart_isChart⟧. Its index at $x$ is $d(f(x), \psi)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex_transportChart⟧. With $\psi$ realizing $d_Y(f(x))$: $d_X(x) \le d_Y(f(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex_le_of_isScDiffeoOn⟧, and with $g$ the reverse ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · proposition_2_24⟧. The text's "from the definitions one deduces immediately" is this construction.

**Definition 2.25.** $\partial X = \{d_X \ge 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.boundary⟧; without boundary means $d_X \equiv 0$, equivalently $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsWithoutBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.isWithoutBoundary_iff⟧. $\partial X$ and the corners $\{d_X \ge 2\}$ are closed, the interior $\{d_X = 0\}$ is open ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.corners⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_corners⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isOpen_interior⟧, and sc-diffeomorphisms preserve $\partial X$ by Proposition 2.24 ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.mem_boundary_iff⟧.

**Lemma 2.26.** For a sub-M-polyfold $A$ and $a \in A$: take a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ realizing $d_X(a)$ and the data at $a$; the sub-chart built on $\varphi$ has the same quadrant $C$ and the same value $\varphi(a)$, so $d_A(a) \le d_C(\varphi(a)) = d_X(a)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · lemma_2_26⟧.

*A retract as an M-polyfold.* A nonempty retract $O$, as a subtype, has the single chart $\mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · LocalModel.selfChart⟧, compatible with itself, and is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · LocalModel.toMPolyfold⟧ (Hausdorff and paracompact as a subspace of $E_0$); so is a nonempty relatively open $U \subseteq C$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.toMPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.selfChart_isChart⟧ — the text's $X_C$.

### II.12 The subspaces $E_x$, the cones $C_x$ and the sign arguments

*Coordinates.* For a presentation $T$ of $C$ and $x \in E_0$, the coordinates vanishing at $x$ form a continuous linear surjection $E_0 \to \mathbb R^{I(x)}$, $v \mapsto ((Tv)_i)_{i \in I(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordMapL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordMapL_surjective⟧. Its kernel is $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · minimalSubspaceWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · mem_minimalSubspaceWith⟧, closed ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · isClosed_minimalSubspaceWith⟧, and by the first isomorphism theorem $E_0/E_x \cong \mathbb R^{I(x)}$, so $\dim(E_0/E_x) = d_C(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · finrank_quotient_minimalSubspaceWith⟧. The cone $C_x = \{v : (Tv)_i \ge 0 \text{ for } i \in I(x)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ is convex and closed and contains $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · convex_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · isClosed_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · minimalSubspaceWith_subset_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧. *Approximation*: if $Tx = (a, w)$, the points $T^{-1}(a, w')$ with $w' \in W_1$ (resp. $W_\infty$) converge to $x$ as $w' \to w$ and have the same vanishing coordinates, so $x$ is a limit of points on level $1$ (resp. smooth points) of the same index, in $C$ iff $x$ is ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · exists_tendsto_lvl1_degIndexWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_tendsto_smooth_degIndexWith⟧.

*Density on level $1$.* For a continuous linear $L : E_0 \to V$, $V$ finite-dimensional, the level-$1$ points of $\ker L$ are dense in $\ker L$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · ScBanach.subset_closure_ker_inter_range_toBase⟧. The image $S$ of $E_1$ is dense in $E_0$; $L$ maps $S$ onto the finite-dimensional $L(S)$, which has a linear, hence continuous, right inverse $g$ with values in $S$. For $v \in \ker L$ take $u_k \in S$ with $u_k \to v$; then $L(u_k) \to 0$, $g(L(u_k)) \to 0$, and $u_k - g(L(u_k)) \in S \cap \ker L$ converges to $v$. This is the text's "the closure of $(T^R_xO)_\infty$ is $T^R_xO$" in the form the proofs need; the level-$1$ points of $C_x$ are dense in $C_x$ likewise ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · partialQuadrantAtWith_subset_closure⟧.

*The two-sided sign argument.* Let $f$ be sc¹ on $U$ relatively open in $C$, with values in $C'$, $x \in U_1$ and $v \in E_1$ with $\iota_1 v \in E_x$. Then $x + tv \in U_1$ for $|t|$ small: the coordinates in $I(x)$ stay $0$, the others stay positive, and $U_1$ is relatively open ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · eventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet⟧. For $j$ with $(T'f(x))_j = 0$ the real function $g(t) = (T'f(\iota_1(x + tv)))_j$ is $\ge 0$ near $0$ (values in $C'$), vanishes at $0$, and has derivative $(T' Df(x)v)_j$ at $0$ (Definition 1.14's derivative along $E_1$, composed with the path); a local minimum has zero derivative ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LocalExtr/Basic · IsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero⟧. So $Df(x)v \in E'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsSc1With.deriv_mem_minimalSubspace_of_lvl1⟧, and by density and continuity of $Df(x)$ on $E_0$, $Df(x)$ maps $E_x$ into $E'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsSc1With.mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧.

*The one-sided sign argument.* For $v \in E_1$ with $\iota_1 v \in C_x$, $x + tv \in U_1$ for small $t \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · eventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet_of_cone⟧, the same $g$ is $\ge 0$ on $[0, \varepsilon)$ with $g(0) = 0$, so its one-sided derivative is $\ge 0$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · nonneg_of_hasDerivWithinAt_Ici⟧; hence $Df(x)v \in C'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsSc1With.deriv_mem_partialQuadrant_of_lvl1⟧, and $Df(x)$ maps $C_x$ into $C'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsSc1With.mapsTo_partialQuadrant⟧. These are the derivative-level content of Lemma 2.29 (1) and (2); the lemma itself, about sc-smooth paths, is not formalized.

*The chain rule at a point.* For sc¹ maps $f$, $g$ on relatively open sets with $f(U) \subseteq U'$, $Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = D(g \circ f)(x)$ at $x \in U_1$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_apply⟧; if $g \circ f = \mathrm{id}$ on $U$ then $g_1(f_1(x)) = x$ and $Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · levelMap_comp_eq_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_eq_self⟧.

### II.13 Proposition 2.30, Theorem 2.31, Corollary 2.32

**Definition 2.27, Remark 2.28.** For a retraction $r$, a presentation $T$ and $x \in O_1$: $T^R_xO := Dr(x)E_0 \cap E_x$ and $C_xO := Dr(x)E_0 \cap C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · reducedTangentSpaceWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · partialConeWith⟧, defined at every point on level $1$; $T^R_xO \subseteq C_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · reducedTangentSpaceWith_subset_partialConeWith⟧. The number $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ is $\dim(A/(A \cap B))$ for $A = T_xO$, $B = E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim⟧; since $A \to E_0/E_x$ has kernel $A \cap E_x$, it is at most $d_C(x)$ and finite ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim_inf_minimalSubspace_le⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim_reducedTangentSpaceWith_le⟧.

*Germs between retracts.* A germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between $O = r(U)$ and $O' = r'(U')$ is a pair $F$, $G$ with $F \circ r$, $G \circ r'$ sc¹ (sc¹ suffices here; the text has sc-smooth), $F(O) \subseteq O'$, $G(O') \subseteq O$, inverse to each other on $O$, $O'$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm⟧; an sc-smooth map between retracts with an sc-smooth inverse is one ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsScSmoothRetractMap.isDiffeoGerm⟧, and two compatible charts give one between the overlap retracts, with the restricted retractions ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MChart.Compatible.isDiffeoGerm⟧. Since $(G \circ r') \circ (F \circ r) = r$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.comp_eq⟧, the chain rule at $x \in O_1$, $y = (F \circ r)_1(x) \in O'_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.image_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.image_image⟧, gives
$$D(G \circ r')(y)\,D(F \circ r)(x) = Dr(x),\qquad D(F \circ r)(x)\,D(G \circ r')(y) = Dr'(y)$$
⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_inv_deriv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_deriv_inv⟧. So $D := D(F \circ r)(x)$ maps $T_xO$ into $T_yO'$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mem_range⟧, and by the sign arguments for $F \circ r$ (with values in $O' \subseteq C'$) it maps $E_x$ into $E'_y$ and $C_x$ into $C'_y$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mapsTo_partialQuadrant⟧.

**Proposition 2.30.** $D(T^R_xO) = T^R_yO'$ and $D(C_xO) = C_yO'$, with $Tf(x) = D$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · proposition_2_30_reduced⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · proposition_2_30_cone⟧. "$\subseteq$": $D$ maps $T_xO$ into $T_yO'$ and $E_x$ (resp. $C_x$) into $E'_y$ (resp. $C'_y$). "$\supseteq$": for $w \in T^R_yO'$, the vector $D' w$, $D' = D(G \circ r')(y)$, lies in $T_xO$ and in $E_x$ by the same facts for the inverse germ, and $D(D' w) = Dr'(y) w = w$ because $w$ is in the range of the projection $Dr'(y)$. This proof does not pass through Lemma 2.29.

*The core of Theorem 2.31.* Along a germ $F$, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_{C'}(F(x))$ for $x \in O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.quotDim_le⟧. With $P = Dr(x)$, $P' = Dr'(y)$: $D$ maps $T_x = PE$ into $T_y = P'E'$ and $D'$ maps back, $D'D = P$ is the identity on $T_x$ and $DD' = P'$ the identity on $T_y$. The map $\Phi : T_x \to T_y/(T_y \cap E'_y)$, $v \mapsto [Dv]$, is onto ($[w] = \Phi(D'w)$) with kernel $T_x \cap E_x$ ($Dv \in E'_y$ implies $v = D'Dv \in E_x$). Hence $T_x/T^R_x \cong T_y/T^R_y$, which embeds in $E'_0/E'_y$, of dimension $d_{C'}(y)$. The same argument with $U_0$ relatively open in $C$ in place of the retract $O$ is the form used for Corollary 2.32 and Theorem 1.25 ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · degIndexWith_le_of_germ⟧: there $D'D = \mathrm{id}$, so $E_0/E_x \cong T_y/T^R_y \hookrightarrow E'_0/E'_y$ and $d_C(x) \le d_{C'}(F(x))$.

**Theorem 2.31.** Let $\varphi$ be a chart of an M-polyfold around $x$ with $\varphi(x) = \iota_1 z$, $r$ a retraction onto its model and $T$ a presentation. For every other chart $\psi$ around $x$, the overlaps are $O \cap W$ and $O' \cap W'$, the transition maps form a germ between the restricted retractions, and the restricted retraction has the same derivative at $z$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.scDeriv_restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · reducedTangentSpaceWith_restrict⟧; so the core gives $\dim(T_zO/T^R_zO) \le d(x, \psi)$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.quotDim_le_chartDegIndex⟧. Taking $\psi$ realizing $d_X(x)$: $\dim(T_zO/T^R_zO) \le d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · theorem_2_31⟧. For a retract $O$ as an M-polyfold with the chart $\mathrm{id}$ this is the text's statement $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_O(x)$, at points on level $1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · theorem_2_31_retract⟧. The text instead reduces to a chart realizing $d_O(x)$ and counts linearly independent $\mathbb R^d$-components; the quotient isomorphism makes the reduction unnecessary. The second statement (equality makes $C_xO$ a partial quadrant) is not formalized: it needs the sc-structure of $T_xO$ and smooth lifts of a basis of $T_xO/T^R_xO$.

**Corollary 2.32.** Let $U$ be nonempty and relatively open in $C$, and $X_U$ its M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · corollary_2_32⟧. The chart $\mathrm{id}$ gives $d_{X_U} \le d_C$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.degIndex_le⟧. At a point $x$ on level $1$, a chart $\psi$ realizing $d_{X_U}(x)$ is compatible with $\mathrm{id}$, so $F = \psi$ (on $U_0 = \operatorname{dom}\psi$, relatively open in $C$) and $G = \psi^{-1}$ form a germ from $U_0$ to the retract $\psi(V)$, and the core gives $d_C(x) \le d_{C'}(\psi(x)) = d_{X_U}(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.degIndex_le_degIndex_of_lvl1⟧. For a general $x$, approximate by level-$1$ points $\sigma_i \in U$ with $d_C(\sigma_i) = d_C(x)$ (§II.12); by Lemma 2.23, $d_{X_U}(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(x)$ eventually, so $d_C(x) = d_C(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(x)$. The text approximates by smooth points; level $1$ suffices. **Theorem 1.25** (Part I, §I.19) is proved in the same file by the same argument for a germ between relatively open subsets of two quadrants ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · theorem_1_25_lvl1⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · theorem_1_25⟧.

### II.14 Tame retractions; Propositions 2.35 and 2.36

**Definition 2.33.** $C_e$ and $E_e$ are the cone and subspace of §II.12 for the presentation $T$. They do not depend on it: for two presentations $T$, $T'$ of $C$ and $e \in C$, $v \in E_e$ (for $T$) gives $e + tv \in C$ for $|t|$ small ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · eventually_add_smul_mem_of_minimalSubspace⟧; for $j$ with $(T'e)_j = 0$, $(T'(e + tv))_j = t(T'v)_j \ge 0$ for $t = \pm\delta/2$, so $(T'v)_j = 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · minimalSubspaceWith_le⟧; by symmetry the two subspaces agree ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · minimalSubspaceWith_eq⟧. This is the argument of Lemma 1.24.

**Definition 2.34.** $r$ is *tame for $T$* if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ on $U$ and (2) at every smooth $x \in O_1$ some $A \le E_x$ makes $E = Dr(x)E_0 \oplus A$ an sc-splitting ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.IsTameWith⟧; *tame* if tame for every presentation ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.IsTame⟧, and by the independence of $E_x$ tameness for one presentation suffices ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame⟧. A *tame retract* is the retract of a tame retraction ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsTameRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsTameRetract.isScRetract⟧. Identities of relatively open sets are tame ($T_xU = E$, $A = 0$) ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.id_isTame⟧, and restrictions of tame retractions to $U \cap r^{-1}(V)$ are tame (same derivatives) ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.restrict⟧.

**Proposition 2.35.** *$Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$ for every retraction at every $x \in O_1$*: the two-sided sign argument for $r$, with $r(x) = x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧. At a smooth $x$, $Dr(x)$ is an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScOperator_scDeriv⟧, so $E = Dr(x)E \oplus (1 - Dr(x))E$ is an sc-splitting ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. *The proposition* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_35⟧: with $A \le E_x$ from tameness (2), $E_0 = Dr(x)E_0 \oplus A$ algebraically (the level-$0$ part of the sc-splitting); write $v = t + a$; then $(1 - Dr(x))v = (1 - Dr(x))a = a - Dr(x)a \in E_x$, because $a \in E_x$ and $Dr(x)a \in E_x$. Only condition (2) is used; the text uses condition (1) for $Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$. In coordinates: $\lambda_j(Dr(x)v) = \lambda_j(v)$ for $j \in I(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧.

**Proposition 2.36.** *(13) at smooth points.* If $V = A' \oplus B$ and $B \le K$, then $A'/(A' \cap K) \cong V/K$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · quotDim_eq_finrank_quotient_of_isCompl⟧; with $A' = T_xO$, $B = A$ and $K = E_x$ this gives $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = \dim(E_0/E_x) = d_C(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · quotDim_reducedTangentSpaceWith_eq⟧ — the text's equations (15)–(16). *A tame chart realizes the index* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith⟧: let $\varphi$ be a chart of any M-polyfold whose model has a tame retraction $r$. At $y$ with $\varphi(y)$ smooth, $d(y, \varphi) = \dim(T/T^R) \le d_X(y)$ by Theorem 2.31, and $d_X(y) \le d(y, \varphi)$ by definition. At a general $y$, with $\varphi(y) = o$, approximate $o$ by smooth points $\sigma_i$ of $C$ with the same vanishing coordinates; then $r(\sigma_i)$ are smooth points of $O$ (an $\mathrm{sc}^0$ map preserves smoothness ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · IsSc0.mem_smooth⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_smoothLvl_one_of_mem_smooth⟧) converging to $r(o) = o$, with $d_C(r(\sigma_i)) = d_C(\sigma_i) = d_C(o)$ by tameness (1); so the points $\varphi^{-1}(r(\sigma_i))$ converge to $y$ and have $d_X = d(\cdot, \varphi) = d_C(o)$, and Lemma 2.23 gives $d_C(o) \le d_X(y)$. For charts of the structure modelled on a tame retract ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameRetract⟧. Applied to the retract itself as an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.toLocalModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.degIndex_toMPolyfold_of_isTameWith⟧: (14) $d_O = d_C$ on $O$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_36_degIndex⟧ and (13) $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x) = d_C(x)$ at smooth points ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_36⟧. This is the text's proof, generalized from the retract to any chart; Proposition 2.42 needs the general form.

*Splitting off finitely many coordinates.* Let $B \le A$ be sc-subspaces of $E$, $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_d$ continuous functionals on $E_0$ with $B = A \cap \bigcap_j \ker \ell_j$, and $e_1, \dots, e_d \in A$ smooth with $\ell_i(e_j) = \delta_{ij}$. Each $e_j$ has a lift to every level $m$, compatible with the inclusions ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · smoothLift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · incl_smoothLift⟧. On level $m$ the maps $v \mapsto ((\ell_j v)_j,\ v - \sum_j \ell_j(v) e_j)$ and $(a, u) \mapsto u + \sum_j a_j e_j$ are continuous linear $A_m \to \mathbb R^d \times B_m$ and back ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitFwd⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitBwd⟧ — the bracket lies in $B$ because every $\ell_i$ kills it ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · sub_sum_mem⟧ — and mutually inverse ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitBwd_splitFwd⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitFwd_splitBwd⟧; they commute with the inclusions, so they form an sc-isomorphism $A \cong \mathbb R^d \oplus B$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitIso⟧, $A$ and $B$ with the sc-structures induced from $E$ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScBanach.ofSubspace⟧. It carries $\{v \in A : \ell_j(v) \ge 0\ \forall j\}$ onto $[0, \infty)^d \oplus B$, so that set is a partial quadrant in $A$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · isPartialQuadrant_ofSubspace⟧. This is the map $S$ of the proof of Theorem 2.31, with the $e_j$ smooth as the exposition requires.

**Proposition 2.36, the remaining statements** ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · proposition_2_36_partialCone⟧. Let $r$ be tame for $T$, $x \in O_1$ smooth, $P = Dr(x)$ and $I(x) = \{i_1, \dots, i_d\}$. $T_xO = PE$ is an sc-subspace, the range of the sc-projection $P$ (Proposition 2.35 above) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. The vectors $\hat e_j := P(T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0))$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordVec⟧ lie in $T_xO$; they are smooth, because $T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)$ is smooth ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · coordVec_mem_smooth⟧ and $P$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScOperator_scDeriv⟧ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScOperator.mapsTo_smoothLvl⟧; and $\lambda_{i_k}(\hat e_j) = \lambda_{i_k}(T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)) = \delta_{jk}$ by Proposition 2.35 in coordinates ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧. By definition $T^R_xO = T_xO \cap \bigcap_k \ker \lambda_{i_k}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordL⟧. *$T^R_xO$ is an sc-subspace.* It is closed, as an intersection of closed subspaces ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · isClosed_minimalSubspaceWith⟧. For the density of smooth points, let $u \in T^R_xO \cap E_m$ with $Tu = (a, w)$ on level $m$, and put $\phi(w') := P(T^{-1}(a, w'))$, a continuous map $W_m \to E_m$. For smooth $w'$ the point $\phi(w')$ is smooth, lies in $T_xO$, and lies in $E_x$, because $T^{-1}(a, w')$ has the same vanishing coordinates in $I(x)$ as $u$ and $P E_x \subseteq E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧. And $\phi(w) = Pu = u$, since $u \in T_xO$ and $P$ is a projection ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self⟧. As $W_\infty$ is dense in $W_m$, $u$ lies in the closure of $\phi(W_\infty) \subseteq T^R_xO \cap E_\infty$ (this is the exposition's Lemma 3.A (1) in the case at hand). *The quadrant.* The splitting with $A = T_xO$, $B = T^R_xO$, $\ell_j = \lambda_{i_j}$ and $e_j = \hat e_j$ makes $\{v \in T_xO : \lambda_{i_j}(v) \ge 0\ \forall j\}$ a partial quadrant in $T_xO$, and this set is $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x$. The text deduces the claim from the equality case of Theorem 2.31, which needs smooth lifts $\hat v^j$ of a basis of $T_xO/T^R_xO$ (the exposition chooses them by a density argument); for a tame retraction they are the explicit $\hat e_j$, and the general equality case, still not formalized, is not needed.

### II.15 Faces: local geometry, Lemma 2.40, Corollary 2.41, Proposition 2.42

**Definitions 2.37, 2.39.** $X$ is *tame* if an atlas equivalent to its atlas has only tame models ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsTame⟧; charts of an equivalent atlas are charts of the structure ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.isChart_of_mem_equiv⟧, so every point lies in a chart of the structure with a tame model ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart⟧. A *face* is the closure of the connected component in $\{d_X = 1\}$ of a point with $d_X = 1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFace⟧, closed ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFace.isClosed⟧ and inside $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.IsFace.subset_boundary⟧; $X$ is *face-structured* if every $x$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFaceStructured⟧.

*Coordinates of faces.* $I(z) = \{i : \lambda_i(z) = 0\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet⟧ with $d_C = \#I$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · degIndexWith_eq_card_zeroSet⟧; the extended face $f_i$ is the hyperplane $\{\lambda_i = 0\}$, closed ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordHyper⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · isClosed_coordHyper⟧; $I(z) \subseteq I(e)$ for $z$ near $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · eventually_zeroSet_subset⟧. *A connected piece of $\{d_C = 1\}$ lies in one face* (exposition Lemma 4.A): if $S \subseteq C$ is preconnected with $d_C = 1$ on $S$ and $\lambda_i(p) = 0$ at some $p \in S$, then $S \subseteq f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · subset_coordHyper_of_isPreconnected⟧. Points of $S$ have $I = \{i\}$ or $\lambda_i > 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet_eq_singleton⟧, so $S$ is covered by the open sets $u = \{\lambda_l > 0 \text{ for } l \ne i\}$ and $v = \{\lambda_i > 0\}$, which are disjoint on $S$ (a point in both would have $d_C = 0$); preconnectedness puts $S$ in one of them ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Clopen · isPreconnected_iff_subset_of_disjoint⟧, and $p \in u$.

*Rays stay in their face* (exposition Lemma 4.B). If $f$ is sc¹, $x + tv \in U_1$ for small $t \ge 0$ and a functional $L$ vanishes on $f(x + tv)$ for $t \in [0, \varepsilon)$, then $L(Df(x)v) = 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · IsSc1With.apply_deriv_eq_zero_of_ray⟧. Now let $r$ be tame, $x \in O_1$ smooth, $i \in I(x)$, $\lambda_i(y) = 0$ and $\lambda_l(y) > 0$ for the other $l \in I(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ray_zeroSet⟧. For small $\tau > 0$, $x + \tau y \in U$ and $I(x + \tau y) = \{i\}$, so $d_C(r(x + \tau y)) = 1$ by tameness (1), and $I(r(x + \tau y)) \subseteq I(x)$ by continuity of $r$ at $x = r(x)$. The image of $(0, \tau_0]$ under $\tau \mapsto r(x + \tau y)$ is preconnected with $d_C = 1$, so it lies in one $f_j$ with $j \in I(x)$. Differentiating $\lambda_j(r(x + \tau y)) = 0$ at $\tau = 0$ gives $\lambda_j(Dr(x)y) = 0$, and $\lambda_j(Dr(x)y) = \lambda_j(y)$ by Proposition 2.35 ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordL⟧; as $\lambda_l(y) > 0$ for $l \in I(x) \setminus \{i\}$, $j = i$. This is the step of Lemma 2.40 that the text omits, and it needs tameness (2).

*The local structure of a face* (exposition Lemma 4.C) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · local_face_structure⟧. Let $S = \{z \in O : d_C(z) = 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.faceStratum⟧ and $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$. (a) Choose $\varepsilon$ so that $B = B_\varepsilon(e) \cap C \subseteq U$ and $I(z), I(r(z)) \subseteq I(e)$ on $B$. (b) $A_i \cap B = \{z \in B : I(z) = \{i\}\}$ is convex ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · convex_ball_inter_zeroSet_eq⟧, hence connected, and $r$ maps it into $S$; a smooth $u = r(T^{-1}(a, w')) \in O \cap B$ with $I(u) = I(e)$ and the ray of Lemma 4.B from $u$ in the direction $T^{-1}(b, 0)$, $b = 1$ on $I(e) \setminus \{i\}$ and $0$ elsewhere ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordVec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · rayDir⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_lvl1_coordVec⟧, produces a point $p \in S$ with $\lambda_i(p) = 0$ in $r(A_i \cap B)$; so $r(A_i \cap B)$ lies in the component of $S$ through $p$. (c) A point $e' \in f_i \cap B$ is the limit of points of $A_i \cap B$ (perturb the coordinates of $I(e') \setminus \{i\}$ upward), so $r(e')$ lies in the closure of that component.

**Lemma 2.40.** A *face of the retract* is $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$ for a component $\hat F$ of $S$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.IsRetractFace⟧. A component of $S$ through a point with $\lambda_i = 0$ lies in $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · faceStratum_degIndexWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_faceStratum_subset⟧, and a component of $S$ in $f_i$ whose closure contains $e$ is the component of Lemma 4.C at $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_eq_of_mem_closure⟧. *The face through $x \in S$, $\lambda_i(x) = 0$, is the component of $f_i \cap O$ through $x$* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · closure_connectedComponentIn_faceStratum⟧: it is connected, lies in $f_i \cap O$, is closed in it, and is relatively open in it by Lemma 4.C(c); a preconnected subset meeting a relatively clopen set lies in it ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · subset_of_relClopen_of_isPreconnected⟧. Conversely, the component of $f_i \cap O$ through any $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$ is the face through the point $p$ of Lemma 4.C at $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_coordHyper_eq⟧. Together: the faces of the retract are the components of the sets $f_i \cap O$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · lemma_2_40⟧. If the components of $f_i \cap O$ and $f_j \cap O$ through $x$ coincide, a point $z$ of the face in $S$ has $I(z) = \{i\}$ and is a limit of points with $I = \{j\}$, which near $z$ forces $j = i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · lemma_2_40_injective⟧. The faces of the M-polyfold $O$ (Definition 2.39, with $d_O = d_C$ by Proposition 2.36) are exactly the faces of the retract, transferred along the subtype inclusion ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · image_val_connectedComponentIn⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · image_val_closure⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isFace_toMPolyfold_iff⟧.

**Corollary 2.41.** The map $i \mapsto$ (component of $f_i \cap O$ through $x$) sends $I(x)$ onto the faces through $x$ (Lemma 2.40) and is injective (its second statement), so $x$ lies in exactly $\#I(x) = d_C(x)$ faces of the retract ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · corollary_2_41_retract⟧, and the M-polyfold $O$ is face-structured ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isFaceStructured_toMPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · corollary_2_41⟧.

**Proposition 2.42.** Let $X$ be tame. *The global bound* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.faces_encard_le⟧: in a tame chart $\varphi$ around $x$, $o = \varphi(x)$, Lemma 4.C gives for each $i \in I(o)$ a component $\hat F_i$ of $S$ containing all points of $O$ near $o$ with $I = \{i\}$. A face $F = \overline G$ through $x$ has points $y \in G$ near $x$; $d_C(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y) = 1$ (the tame chart realizes $d_X$) and $I(\varphi y) \subseteq I(o)$, so $I(\varphi y) = \{i\}$ for some $i \in I(o)$, and the preconnected set $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_i) \subseteq \{d_X = 1\}$ meets $G$, hence lies in $G$. Distinct faces give distinct $i$; so at most $d_X(x)$ faces pass through $x$. *The local statement*: the tame chart realizes $d_X$ on its domain, the M-polyfold $O$ has $d_O = d_C$ (Proposition 2.36), and $O$ is face-structured (Corollary 2.41) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_42⟧. The neighbourhood $V$ of the text is represented by $O$.

### II.16 Faces are tame sub-M-polyfolds: Propositions 2.43, 2.44 and Theorem 2.45

*The projection onto a face.* $P_i := T^{-1} \circ (a \mapsto a \text{ with } a_i = 0) \circ T$ is an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoordL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoordModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord⟧ which kills the $i$-th coordinate and keeps the others ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_coord⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_coord_self⟧, fixes $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_eq_self⟧ and maps $C$ into $C$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_mem⟧.

**Proposition 2.43, the retraction.** Let $F$ be a face of the retract, through $x \in S$ with $I(x) = \{i\}$, so $F \subseteq f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_43⟧. For each $e \in F$, Lemma 4.C gives $\varepsilon_e$ with $B_e = B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap C \subseteq U$ and $r(z) \in F$ for $z \in B_e \cap f_i$ (the component of Lemma 4.C at $e$ is the one of $F$). Put $U^* := \bigcup_{e \in F} (B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap P_i^{-1}(B_{\varepsilon_e}(e))) \cap C$: relatively open in $C$, contains $F$ (as $P_i e = e$), and for $z \in U^*$ the point $P_i z$ lies in some $B_e \cap f_i$, so $r(P_i z) \in F$. Then $s := r \circ P_i$ is sc-smooth on $U^*$ (chain rule), maps $U^*$ into $F \subseteq U^*$, and fixes $F$; so it is a retraction onto $F$, and $U^* \subseteq U$. The preimages under $P_i$ are needed because $P_i$ need not be norm-decreasing for the norm of $E_0$; the exposition's "$|P_1 z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0$" holds only for special norms. *$F$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$*: in the chart $\mathrm{id}$ of $O$, $s$ restricted to $O \cap U^*$ is an sc-smooth retraction onto $F$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.selfChart_symm_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace⟧.

*The face as a model space.* Insert and delete a coordinate: $\mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^{k+1}$, $b \mapsto (b_1, \dots, 0_i, \dots, b_k)$, and back ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · insertCoordL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · removeCoordL⟧, as sc-operators on $\mathbb R^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · insertCoordModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · removeCoordModel⟧; composed with $T$ they give $\iota : \mathbb R^k \oplus W \to E$ onto $f_i$ and $\pi : E \to \mathbb R^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj⟧, with $\pi\iota = 1$, $\iota\pi = 1$ on $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj_faceIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl_faceProj⟧, $\iota(C') \subseteq C$ and $\pi(C) \subseteq C'$ for $C' = [0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj_mem⟧, and $d_C(y) = d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1$ on $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · degIndexWith_eq_quadrantDeg_faceProj_add_one⟧. The derivative of an sc-operator is itself ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScOperator.scDeriv_eq⟧, and the chain rule at a point holds between arbitrary sc-domains ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · scDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain⟧.

**Proposition 2.43, the tame model** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · proposition_2_43_tameModel⟧. With $U^*$ and $s$ as above, put $U' := \iota^{-1}(U^*)$ (relatively open in $C'$) and $r' := \pi \circ r \circ \iota$ on $U'$. Since $r \circ \iota$ maps $U'$ into $F \subseteq f_i$, where $\iota\pi = 1$, $r'$ is an sc-smooth retraction with retract $\pi(F)$, and $\iota$ maps it back into $F$. *Tameness (1)*: for $z \in U'$, $d_{C'}(r'z) + 1 = d_C(r(\iota z)) = d_C(\iota z) = d_{C'}(z) + 1$. *Tameness (2)*: at a smooth $x \in \pi(F)$, $\iota x$ is a smooth point of $O$ and $Dr'(x)v = \pi(Dr(\iota x)(\iota v))$ by the chain rule; for $j$ with $x_j = 0$ the coordinate $j' = i.\mathrm{succAbove}(j)$ vanishes at $\iota x$, and Proposition 2.35 for $r$ gives $\lambda_{j'}(Dr(\iota x)\iota v) = \lambda_{j'}(\iota v) = v_j$; so $\lambda'_j \circ Dr'(x) = \lambda'_j$, and $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$ is an sc-complement of $T_x\pi(F)$ inside $E'_x$. The exposition instead intersects the complement $A$ of $T_xO$ with $f_1$; that is not needed. And $d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1 = d_C(y)$ on $F$.

**Proposition 2.43, faces are tame** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · LocalModel.proposition_2_43_isTame⟧. For a face $F$ of a tame retract $O$ (paracompact, being closed), the chart $\pi : F \to \pi(F)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChartInv⟧ is compatible with the sub-charts of $F$ built on the chart $\mathrm{id}$ of $O$, its transition maps being the sc-operators $\iota$ and $\pi$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart⟧; a chart compatible with all sub-charts built on one chart of $X$ is a chart of the induced structure, by locality of compatibility ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible⟧. Its model is the tame retract $(\pi(F), C', E')$, so $F$ is tame (a space all of whose points lie in tame charts is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart⟧), and the tame chart realizes the index: $d_F(x) = d_{C'}(\pi x) = d_C(x) - 1 = d_O(x) - 1$ (equation (14) twice). The text calls this last statement obvious.

**Proposition 2.44, first sentence** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.proposition_2_44⟧. In a tame chart $\varphi$ around $x$: $\varphi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$ (Proposition 2.42 with Corollary 2.41), and each face of $O$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold with $d_F + 1 = d_O$, where $d_O(\varphi x) = d_X(x)$.

*The corner as a model space.* For $\sigma \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ list the coordinates outside $\sigma$ as $j \mapsto l_j$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIdx⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIdx_injective⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · exists_cornerIdx⟧. Deleting the coordinates in $\sigma$ and inserting zeros there ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertL⟧ are mutually inverse on $\{a : a_l = 0,\ l \in \sigma\}$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveL_cornerInsertL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertL_cornerRemoveL⟧; as sc-operators on $\mathbb R^{n} \oplus W$ and $\mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveModel⟧, composed with $T$, they give $\iota_\sigma : \mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W \to E$ onto the corner $f_\sigma = \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} f_i$ and $\pi_\sigma : E \to \mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj⟧, with $\pi_\sigma\iota_\sigma = 1$ and $\iota_\sigma\pi_\sigma = 1$ on $f_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj_cornerIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl_cornerProj⟧, $\iota_\sigma(C') \subseteq C$ and $\pi_\sigma(C) \subseteq C'$ for $C' = [0, \infty)^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj_mem⟧, and $d_C(y) = d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma$ on $f_\sigma$: the vanishing coordinates of $y$ are those of $\sigma$ together with the images $l_j$ of the vanishing coordinates of $\pi_\sigma y$, disjointly ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · degIndexWith_eq_quadrantDeg_cornerProj_add_card⟧. The sc-projection $P_\sigma = \iota_\sigma \circ \pi_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill⟧ sets the coordinates in $\sigma$ to zero ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_coord_mem⟧, fixes $f_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_eq_self⟧ and maps $C$ into $C$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_mem⟧. For $\sigma = \{i\}$ these are the $\iota$, $\pi$ and $P_i$ of Proposition 2.43.

*The retraction onto a corner* ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_retraction⟧. Let $r$ be tame for $T$, $o \in O$ and $\sigma \subseteq I(o)$. For each $i \in \sigma$, Lemma 4.C at $o$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · local_face_structure⟧ gives a face $F_i$ of the retract with $o \in F_i \subseteq f_i$, containing a point with $d_C = 1$, and a ball around $o$ in which $r$ maps the points of $C \cap f_i$ into $F_i$. Distinct $i$ give distinct faces: a point $p \in F_i$ with $d_C(p) = 1$ has $I(p) = \{i\}$, so $F_i = F_j$ forces $i = j$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet_eq_singleton⟧. Take a ball $B$ around $o$ inside all these balls with $B \cap C \subseteq U$, an open $W_s$ with $W_s \cap U = r^{-1}(B) \cap U$ (continuity of $r$), and put $V := B \cap P_\sigma^{-1}(B \cap W_s)$, an open set containing $o$ (since $P_\sigma o = o = r(o)$). On $V \cap C$ the map $s := r \circ P_\sigma$ is sc-smooth by the chain rule. For $z \in V \cap C$, $P_\sigma z \in C \cap f_\sigma \cap B$, so $r(P_\sigma z) \in F_i \subseteq f_i$ for every $i \in \sigma$: $s(z) \in O \cap f_\sigma$. Moreover $s(z) \in B$ (as $P_\sigma z \in W_s$), $P_\sigma s(z) = s(z)$, and $s(z) \in W_s$ (as $r(s(z)) = s(z) \in B$); so $s$ maps $V \cap C$ into itself. On $f_\sigma \cap O$, $P_\sigma$ and $r$ are the identity, so $s \circ s = s$: $s$ is an sc-smooth retraction with retract $O \cap V \cap f_\sigma$, and this set equals $O \cap V \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i$ (a point of $O \cap V \cap f_\sigma$ is fixed by $r$, which maps it into each $F_i$; conversely $F_i \subseteq f_i$). The exposition proceeds by induction on $\#\sigma$, identifying the germ of $F_1 \cap F_2$ with a face of $F_1$; the formal proof removes all coordinates of $\sigma$ at once.

*The tame model of a corner* ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_tameModel⟧. Let $s$ be an sc-smooth retraction on $U_s \subseteq U$, equal to $r \circ P_\sigma$ there, with retract $F \subseteq O \cap f_\sigma$; write $U_s = W_0 \cap C$ with $W_0$ open, and put $U' := \iota_\sigma^{-1}(W_0) \cap C'$ and $r' := \pi_\sigma \circ r \circ \iota_\sigma$ on $U'$. For $z \in U'$, $r(\iota_\sigma z) = s(\iota_\sigma z) \in F$ (as $P_\sigma\iota_\sigma = \iota_\sigma$), so $r'$ maps $U'$ into $\pi_\sigma(F) \subseteq U'$; it is sc-smooth by the chain rule and idempotent because $\iota_\sigma\pi_\sigma = 1$ on $F$ and $r = 1$ on $F \subseteq O$; its retract is $\pi_\sigma(F)$. *Tameness (1):* $d_{C'}(r'z) + \#\sigma = d_C(r(\iota_\sigma z)) = d_C(\iota_\sigma z) = d_{C'}(z) + \#\sigma$ (the index formula on $f_\sigma$ twice, and tameness (1) of $r$) ⟦Chapter1/Degeneracy · degIndex_eq⟧. *Tameness (2):* at a smooth $x$ of the retract, $\iota_\sigma x$ is a smooth point of $O$, and $Dr'(x)v = \pi_\sigma(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v)$ by the chain rule between sc-domains ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · scDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScOperator.scDeriv_eq⟧; for $j$ with $x_j = 0$ the coordinate $l_j$ vanishes at $\iota_\sigma x$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · coord_cornerIncl_idx⟧, and Proposition 2.35 gives $\lambda_{l_j}(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v) = \lambda_{l_j}(\iota_\sigma v) = v_j$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧; so $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$ lies in $E'_x$ and is an sc-complement of $T_x\pi_\sigma(F)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. And $d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma = d_C(y)$ for $y \in F$. This is the proof of the tame model of Proposition 2.43 with $\sigma$ in place of $\{i\}$.

**Proposition 2.44, second sentence** ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · MPolyfold.proposition_2_44_corner⟧. Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$, and take a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ of the structure around $x$ with a tame retraction $r$ onto $O$, tame for a presentation $T$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart⟧. The face germs at $x$ are the faces $F_i$, $i \in I(\varphi x)$, of the retract (Corollary 2.41: there are $d_X(x)$ of them), and $\sigma$ is a set of such indices. The retraction onto the corner gives the pairwise distinct faces $F_i \ni \varphi(x)$, $i \in \sigma$, an open $B \ni \varphi(x)$ and $s$ with retract $O \cap B \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i$. Put $A := \{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in B,\ \varphi(y) \in F_i\ \forall i \in \sigma\}$; its germ at $x$ is the germ $F^\sigma_x$. Since $\varphi(A)$ is the retract of $s$, $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold by the local criterion of Theorem 2.45 ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local⟧ (paracompact as every subset ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype⟧). The chart $\pi_\sigma \circ \varphi$ of $A$ onto the retract $\pi_\sigma(\varphi(A))$ of $r'$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart⟧ is compatible with the sub-charts of $A$ built on $\varphi$, its transitions being $\iota_\sigma$ and $\pi_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart⟧, hence a chart of the induced structure ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible⟧; its model is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame⟧, so $A$ is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart⟧. Both tame charts realize the index ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith⟧, so for $a \in A$: $d_A(a) + \#\sigma = d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma\varphi(a)) + \#\sigma = d_C(\varphi(a)) = d_X(a)$; in particular $d_A(x) = d_X(x) - \#\sigma$, and the codimension, the number of quadrant coordinates removed in the tame model, is $\#\sigma$. The text states the proposition without proof.

**Theorem 2.45.** *The interior of a face.* $F \cap \{d_X = 1\} = G$ for $F = \overline G$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.theorem_2_45_interior⟧: at $y \in F$ with $d_X(y) = 1$, in a tame chart with $I(\varphi y) = \{i\}$, all points of $\{d_X = 1\}$ near $y$ lie in $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F)$ for the single component $\hat F$ of Lemma 4.C at $\varphi(y)$, a connected subset of $\{d_X = 1\}$ containing $y$; it meets $G$ (as $y \in \overline G$), hence lies in $G$. *A local criterion for sub-M-polyfolds* ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local⟧: if near each $a \in A$, in a chart $\varphi$, $\varphi(A \cap V)$ agrees on an open $B \ni \varphi(a)$ with the retract of an sc-smooth retraction $s$ contained in $O$, then $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold, with the retraction $\varphi^{-1} \circ s \circ \varphi$ on $V' = \varphi^{-1}(B \cap W_0 \cap s^{-1}(B))$ — shrunk so that $s$ maps it into itself, a step the exposition's "transport by $\varphi^{-1}$" omits. *$G$ is a sub-M-polyfold* ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isSubMPolyfold_interior⟧: at $y \in G$, the local face $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$ agrees with $\varphi(G)$ on the ball of Lemma 4.C (both consist of the points of $S$ there), and Proposition 2.43 gives its retraction. *The face-structured case.* Near $x \in F$, in a tame chart, $\varphi(F)$ agrees on a ball with a face of the retract ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.exists_localFace_of_isFaceStructured⟧: the map $i \mapsto F_i$ (the closure of the component of $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_i)$) from $I(\varphi x)$ to the faces through $x$ is onto (as in Proposition 2.42), and since there are exactly $d_X(x) = \#I(\varphi x)$ faces through $x$, it is injective; so the points of $G$ near $x$ lie in $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_j)$ for the one $j$ with $F = F_j$. Hence $F$ is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isSubMPolyfold_face⟧, and with the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$ onto the restrictions of the tame retractions $r'$ it is tame with $d_X(x) = d_F(x) + 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isTame_face⟧. The local and global face counts of the theorem are Proposition 2.42 and the definition of face-structured.

### II.17 Products and fibred products: Lemma 4.D and Proposition 2.46

*Products of partial quadrants.* For presentations $T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W$ and $T' : E' \cong \mathbb R^{n'} \oplus W'$ of $C$ and $C'$, concatenating the coordinates ($\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^{n'} \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · finAppendL⟧) gives a presentation $E \oplus E' \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'} \oplus (W \oplus W')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · prodPresentation⟧ of $C \times C'$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · prod_eq_prodPresentation⟧, so $C \times C'$ is a partial quadrant ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsPartialQuadrant.prod⟧ and $U \times U'$ is relatively open in it ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod⟧. The vanishing coordinates of $(x, x')$ are those of $x$ followed by those of $x'$, so $d_{C \times C'}(x, x') = d_C(x) + d_{C'}(x')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · degIndexWith_prodPresentation⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · degIndex_prod⟧, and the minimal subspace is $E_x \oplus E'_{x'}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · minimalSubspaceWith_prodPresentation⟧.

*Products of retractions.* $f \times f'$ is sc-smooth when $f$ and $f'$ are ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSmooth.prodMap⟧, with derivative $Df(x) \times Df'(x')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · scDeriv_prodMap⟧; so $r \times r'$ is an sc-smooth retraction ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.prod⟧ with retract $O \times O'$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.prod_retract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScRetract.prod⟧, and products of sc-smooth maps between retracts are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSmoothRetractMap.prodMap⟧. Products of sc-subspaces and of sc-splittings are again such ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSubspace.prod⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSplitting.prod⟧; hence if $r$, $r'$ are tame for $T$, $T'$, then $r \times r'$ is tame for the product presentation ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.prod⟧: (1) is the additivity of the index, and for (2) the complement of $T_{(x, x')}(O \times O') = T_xO \oplus T_{x'}O'$ is $A \oplus A'$ inside $E_x \oplus E'_{x'}$.

**Lemma 4.D (the product M-polyfold).** $X \times Y$ is paracompact, being metrizable by Theorem 2.16 ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_prod⟧. The product charts ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.prod⟧ have the product retracts as models ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · LocalModel.prod⟧, their overlaps are products ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.overlap_prod⟧, and products of compatible charts are compatible ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.Compatible.prod⟧; so they form an atlas of an M-polyfold structure on $X \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.prod⟧, in which products of charts of the factors are charts ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsChart.prod⟧. In a product chart the index is additive ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex_prod⟧; choosing charts that realize $d_X(x)$ and $d_Y(y)$ gives $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) \le d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le⟧. If $X$ and $Y$ are tame, products of tame charts are tame charts, so $X \times Y$ is tame, and since a tame chart realizes the index (§II.14), $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isTame_prod⟧. The text's "$d_{X \times Y} = d_X + d_Y$" is thus a statement about tame spaces. The projections are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_fst⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_snd⟧ and so is the pairing $z \mapsto (f(z), g(z))$ of sc-smooth maps ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.prodMk⟧.

**Proposition 2.46.** A *local sc-diffeomorphism* $f : X \to Z$ is read as: every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ that $f$ maps sc-diffeomorphically onto an open subset ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo⟧; such an $f$ is continuous and sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.continuous⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isScSmoothMap⟧. The fibred product $X {}_f\times_g Y = \{(x, y) : f(x) = g(y)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredProduct⟧ is closed in $X \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isClosed_fibredProduct⟧, hence paracompact, which the text does not mention. *Sub-M-polyfold.* Near $(x, y)$, with $f|_U : U \to W$ an sc-diffeomorphism and $V = g^{-1}(W)$, the map $R(x', y') = ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')$ on $U \times V$ is sc-smooth, idempotent, with image the fibred product near $(x, y)$; in a product chart it is an sc-smooth retraction ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredSubDataL⟧, and so the fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct⟧ (symmetrically when $g$ is the local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredSubDataR⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct'⟧). *$\pi_2$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism.* On the fibred product near $(x, y)$, $\pi_2$ is sc-smooth with inverse $y' \mapsto ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')$, a pairing of sc-smooth maps with values in the fibred product, hence sc-smooth into the sub-M-polyfold by Proposition 2.21 (2) ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_snd_fibredProduct⟧; symmetrically for $\pi_1$ when $g$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_fst_fibredProduct⟧. The exposition factors this inverse through $y' \mapsto (x, y')$, which is not sc-smooth unless $x$ is a smooth point (a constant map is sc⁰ only when its value lies in $X_\infty$); the formula above has the same values and avoids it. *The index.* Proposition 2.24 along $\pi_2$ gives $d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_Y(y)$ for arbitrary $Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_snd⟧, and along $\pi_1$, when $g$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, $= d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_fst⟧. *Tameness.* If $Y$ is tame, the charts $\psi \circ \pi_2$, $\psi$ a tame chart of $Y$ restricted to $g^{-1}(W)$, are charts of the fibred product with tame models ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isTame_fibredProduct⟧. Together: Proposition 2.46 ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.proposition_2_46⟧, and in its last statement $d = d_X = d_Y$ for arbitrary $X$, $Y$ and, for tame $X$, $Y$, $2d = d_{X \times Y}$ by Lemma 4.D ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.proposition_2_46_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧.

### II.18 Strong bundle retractions (Definitions 2.47–2.49)

*$U \triangleleft F$.* The double filtration is $U_m \times F_k$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · doubleLevel⟧. $C \times F_0$ is a partial quadrant in $E \oplus F$, through $(\mathbb R^n \oplus W) \oplus F \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus (W \oplus F)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · prodQuadrantIso⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsPartialQuadrant.prod_univ⟧, and $U \times F_0$ is relatively open in it ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod_univ⟧ — so "sc-smooth on $(U \triangleleft F)[i] = U \oplus F^i$" makes sense (exposition Lemma 1.B of Chapter 1). Pairings of $\mathrm{sc}^k$ maps are $\mathrm{sc}^k$, with the tangent map rearranged by an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · scPair⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · tangentProdSwap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsSck.scPair⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsScSmooth.scPair⟧, and the projections and inclusions of products are sc-operators ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodFstOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodSndOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodInlOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodShiftInclOp⟧.

**Definition 2.47.** A strong bundle map maps $U \times F_0$ into $U' \times F'_0$, has first component independent of $h$ and second linear in $h$, maps $U_m \times F_k$ into $U'_m \times F'_k$ for $k \le m + 1$, is sc-smooth on $U \times F_0$, and its fibre-lifted map on $U \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · shiftFiber⟧ is sc-smooth for $E \oplus F^1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleMap⟧; a strong bundle retraction is an idempotent one ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleRetraction⟧. *Lemma 5.A.* The base $r(u) = R(u, 0)_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleMap.base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.apply_fst⟧ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U$: sc-smooth as $R$ composed with $u \mapsto (u, 0)$ and the first projection, idempotent by the first component of $R \circ R = R$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.baseRetraction⟧. For $u \in O$, $R(u, h) = (u, \Gamma(u, h))$, so the second component of $R \circ R = R$ reads $\Gamma(u, \Gamma(u, h)) = \Gamma(u, h)$: $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ is a projection ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.fiber_idem⟧. $R$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U \times F_0$ in $C \times F_0$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetraction⟧ and, through the lift of the fibre component to $F_1$ (possible since $R$ preserves the double filtration at $(0, 1)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.snd_mem_range⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toBase_shiftFiber_snd⟧), on $U \times F_1$ for $E \oplus F^1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetractionOne⟧.

**Definition 2.48.** $K$ is a local strong bundle retract if $K = R(U \times F_0)$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleRetract⟧, with $K_{m,k}$, $K[i]_m$ and $K[1] \subseteq E_0 \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongLevel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongLevelShift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongShiftOne⟧ and the projection $p$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongProj⟧. $K = \{(u, h) : u \in O, \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.mem_image_iff⟧. *Lemma 5.B.* $K[1]$ is the image of $R$ on $U \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetractionOne_retract⟧, so $K$ and $K[1]$ are retracts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScRetract_one⟧; the base $p(K)$ is $O$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.base_eq⟧; and $p : K[i] \to O$ is sc-smooth, because $p \circ R = r \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ is ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst_one⟧, as is the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_shiftIncl⟧.

**Definition 2.49.** An sc-smooth section is sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ into $(K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScSmoothSection⟧; an sc⁺-section is sc-smooth into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScPlusSection⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScPlusSection.mem⟧. Composed with the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ (Theorem 2.8), an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsScPlusSection.isScSmoothSection⟧.

### II.19 Strong bundles over M-polyfolds (Definitions 2.50–2.53)

**Definition 2.50.** For $P : Y \to X$ with linear structures on the fibres, a strong bundle chart is a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ (of the structure — the text says only "a homeomorphism onto $O$"), a strong bundle retraction $R$ on $U \subseteq C$ with base retract $O$, and a homeomorphism $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K$ with $\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))$, linear on fibres ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.K⟧. $K$ is a local strong bundle retract and a retract on $[0]$ and $[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isStrongBundleRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.model⟧, the source $P^{-1}(V)$ is open ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isOpen_source⟧, $\Phi(P^{-1}(V)) = K$ and $p(K) = O$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.image_source⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.base_K⟧. "Bounded on the fibres" needs no hypothesis: the restriction of the continuous $\Phi$ to a fibre is continuous ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.continuous_fiber⟧. Two charts are compatible if the transitions $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.overlap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.transition⟧ and back are sc-smooth between the overlaps on $[0]$ and, fibre-lifted, on $[1]$, and carry fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.symm⟧; the last condition, implicit in the text, is what makes $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ the restriction of $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$. Atlases and their equivalence ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleAtlas⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv⟧; Banachable fibres ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsBanachable⟧.

**Definition 2.51.** A strong bundle is a continuous surjection with Banachable fibres and a strong bundle atlas, $Y$ Hausdorff paracompact ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle⟧. Each $\Phi$ is a chart of $Y$ with model $(K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.toMChart⟧, compatibility of strong bundle charts on $[0]$ is compatibility of these charts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.toMChart⟧, and they form the atlas of the M-polyfold $Y[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.atlas0⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.toMPolyfold0⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.isChart_toMChart⟧. $P : Y[0] \to X$ is sc-smooth: in the charts $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ it is $p : K \to O$ (Lemma 5.B), and one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj⟧. The double filtration $Y_{m,k}$ is defined through all the charts of the atlas around a point ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.doubleLevel⟧.

*$Y_{m,k}$ does not depend on the chart* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff⟧. Let $y$ lie in the domain of a chart $\Phi$ of the atlas with $\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k$, $k \le m + 1$, and let $\Phi'$ be another chart around $y$; then $\Phi'(y) = (\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})(\Phi(y))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.transition_apply⟧. *The base component:* $\Phi'(y)_1 = \varphi'(\varphi^{-1}(\Phi(y)_1))$, and the base transition, sc-smooth and so $\mathrm{sc}^0$, maps points of level $m$ to points of level $m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.transition_apply⟧. *The fibre component, $k \le m$:* $\Phi(y)$ lies on level $k$ of $E \oplus F$ (levels decrease ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.range_toBase_mono⟧), and the $[0]$-transition, $\mathrm{sc}^0$ on the overlap retract ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap⟧, keeps it on level $k$. *The case $k = m + 1$:* the fibre component of $\Phi(y)$ lies in $F_1$, so its lift $\Phi(y)[1]$ to $E_0 \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.toBase_liftOne⟧ is a point of level $m$ of $E \oplus F^1$ (level $m$ of $F^1$ is $F_{m+1}$ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScBanach.shiftScale_toBase⟧); the $[1]$-transition, $\mathrm{sc}^0$ for $E \oplus F^1$ on the overlap ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap_one⟧, keeps it on level $m$, and its value is the lift $\Phi'(y)[1]$, because the $F_1$-condition of compatibility puts the fibre component of $\Phi'(y)$ in $F'_1$. So $\Phi'(y) \in E'_m \times F'_{m+1}$. The case $k \le m$ uses the $[0]$-transition only; the case $k = m + 1$ uses exactly the $F_1$-condition made explicit in Definition 2.50.

*The set $Y[1]$ and its topology.* $Y_{0,1}$ is the set of points whose fibre component lies in $F_1$ in every chart of the atlas around them ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneSet⟧; by the $F_1$-condition one chart suffices ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff⟧. $Y[1]$ is $Y_{0,1}$ as a type ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.One⟧ with the topology generated by the sets $\{y \in \operatorname{dom}\Phi : \Phi(y)[1] \in W\}$, $W$ open in $E_0 \times F_1$, as for $X_m$ in §2.2 ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isOpen_one_basic⟧. The inclusion $Y[1] \to Y$ is continuous ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.continuous_oneVal⟧: inside the domain of a chart $\Phi$, an open subset of $Y$ is the preimage under $\Phi$ of an open $W \subseteq E_0 \times F_0$ ($\Phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $K$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.exists_isOpen_image_eq⟧), and its points in $Y[1]$ form the basic set of $(1 \times \iota)^{-1}(W)$. A continuous injection into the Hausdorff space $Y$ makes $Y[1]$ Hausdorff ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff · T2Space.of_injective_continuous⟧.

*The charts $\Phi[1]$* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart⟧. $y \mapsto \Phi(y)[1]$ maps $P^{-1}(V) \cap Y[1]$ into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.liftOne_mem⟧, with inverse $z \mapsto \Phi^{-1}(z_1, \iota z_2)$, a point of $Y_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.symm_mem_oneSet⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChartInv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.liftOne_symm⟧. It is continuous by the definition of the topology. Its inverse is continuous: a basic open set $\{\Phi'(y)[1] \in W\}$ pulls back to the set of $z \in K[1]$ in the $[1]$-part of the overlap with $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1](z) \in W$; the overlap is $K \cap W_0$ for an open $W_0$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.overlap_eq_inter⟧ and the $[1]$-transition is continuous on it, so this set is open in $K[1]$. The overlap of $\Phi[1]$ and $\Phi'[1]$ is the $[1]$-part of the overlap of $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_overlap⟧, and their transition map is the $[1]$-transition $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_transition⟧, sc-smooth in both directions by Definition 2.50; so the charts $\Phi[1]$ are compatible ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_compatible⟧ and form an atlas of $Y[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.atlas1⟧. $Y[1]$ is metrizable: $P$ restricted to $Y[1]$ is continuous into the paracompact Hausdorff $X$, and over the domain $V$ of a chart of $X$ its preimage is the source of a chart $\Phi[1]$, homeomorphic to a retract and so metrizable ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MChart.metrizableSpace_source⟧; the pull-back form of Smirnov's theorem applies ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.metrizableSpace_one⟧. Hence $Y[1]$ is paracompact ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.paracompactSpace_one⟧, which an M-polyfold must be and the text does not mention, and **$Y[1]$ is an M-polyfold** ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.toMPolyfold1⟧ whose charts include the $\Phi[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isChart_oneChart⟧.

*$P[1]$ and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$.* In the charts $\Phi[1]$ and $\varphi$, $P[1]$ is the projection $K[1] \to O$ of Lemma 5.B ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst_one⟧, and one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts⟧; so **$P[1] : Y[1] \to X$ is sc-smooth** ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj1⟧. In the charts $\Phi[1]$ and $\Phi$ the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is $(u, h) \mapsto (u, \iota h)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_shiftIncl⟧, so it is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_oneVal⟧ (not stated in the text; it gives that an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section).

**Definition 2.52.** A section has $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsSection⟧; it is sc-smooth if sc-smooth into $Y[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection⟧, and an sc⁺-section if in every chart its fibre values lie in $F_1$ and its fibre-lifted representative ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.localRepOne⟧ is sc-smooth into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection⟧. *This is the text's definition* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_iff⟧: $f$ is an sc⁺-section iff it is a section and $f = \iota \circ g$ for an sc-smooth $g : X \to Y[1]$, $\iota$ the inclusion. Forward: the values of $f$ lie in $Y_{0,1}$ (one chart suffices), which defines $g$; on the domain of a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ under a strong bundle chart $\Phi$, $g = \Phi[1]^{-1} \circ (\text{the local representative}) \circ \varphi$, which gives the continuity of $g$, and the representative of $g$ in the charts $\varphi$, $\Phi[1]$ is the chart-wise representative, sc-smooth by hypothesis. Backward: the fibre values lie in $F_1$ because $g$ takes values in $Y_{0,1}$, and the chart-wise representative is the representative of $g$ in $\varphi$, $\Phi[1]$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.14 (a chart with empty domain is handled separately).

**Definition 2.53.** $f^*Y = \{(z, y) : P(y) = f(z)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackSpace⟧ with the projections ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackProj'⟧, $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_comm⟧; $P_f$ is continuous and $f^*Y$ closed in $Z \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · continuous_pullbackProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isClosed_pullbackSpace⟧.

### II.20 Proposition 2.54: the pull-back strong bundle

*The pulled-back retraction.* For a retraction $r'$ on $U'$ and $g : O' \to O$ sc-smooth between retracts, $R_g(w, h) := (r'(w), \Gamma(g(r'(w)), h))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackRetraction⟧, where $g(r'(w)) \in O \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_mem_O⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_mem_U⟧. It is a strong bundle retraction ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isStrongBundleRetraction_pullback⟧: it maps $U' \times F_0$ into itself; its first component does not depend on $h$ and its second is linear in $h$; it preserves the double filtration ($r'$ and $g \circ r'$ preserve levels, and $R$ preserves the double filtration); on $[0]$ it is the pairing of $r' \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ with the second component of $R \circ ((g \circ r') \circ \mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_2)$, sc-smooth by the chain rule and the pairing lemma, and likewise on $[1]$; and $R_g \circ R_g = R_g$ because $r' \circ r' = r'$ and $\Gamma(o, \cdot)$ is a projection for $o = g(r'(w)) \in O$ (Lemma 5.A). Its image is $K_g = \{(w, h) : w \in O', (g(w), h) \in K\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_image⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isStrongBundleRetract_pullback⟧.

*The fibres.* $P_f^{-1}(z) \to P^{-1}(f(z))$, $(z, y) \mapsto y$, is a bijection ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiberEquiv⟧; transporting the linear structure along it ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiber_addCommGroup⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiber_module⟧ makes it a linear homeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiberCLE⟧, so the fibres of $f^*Y$ are Banachable.

*The charts.* The data: a strong bundle chart $c$ of $Y$, a chart $\psi$ of $Z$ with $f(\operatorname{dom}\psi) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$, a retraction $r_Z$ onto the model of $\psi$, and the sc-smoothness of $g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g_smooth⟧. The chart $\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))$ maps $P_f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)$ into $K_g$ — because $\Phi(y) = (g(\psi(z)), \cdot) \in K$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.mem_Kg⟧ — with inverse $(w, h) \mapsto (\psi^{-1}(w), \Phi^{-1}(g(w), h))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.symm_mem_pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.invFun⟧; both are continuous, it covers $\psi$ and is linear on fibres, so it is a strong bundle chart of $f^*Y$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.toChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.image_eq_Kg⟧.
