Near a zero $x_0$ in good position (with $f$ of tame germ data) there is an open $V$ such that every zero in $V$ is in good position, $S = S_f \cap V$ is a smooth submanifold (§V.17), and at every zero $y \in V$: $(f, y)$ is in general position iff $S$ is in general position at $y$ (Definition 4.21, Part IV). Since $T_zS = \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ in every chart, an sc-complement of $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ inside $T^R_zO$ *is* an sc-complement of $T_zS$ inside $T^R_zO$. Definition 4.21 is chart independent (Part IV) ⟦Chapter4/Submanifolds · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGeneralPositionChart⟧, so Definition 5.17 is too, at these zeros.

**From submanifold general position to good position** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGoodPositionGermTame_of_isGeneralPositionAt⟧. If $f'(y)$ is onto and a smooth submanifold $A \subseteq S_f$ is in general position at $y$, then in the tame chart of the germ data $T_zA \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ (§V.17) ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.linKer_le⟧ and $T_zA + T^R_zO = T_zO$; so $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) + T^R_zO = T_zO$, the kernel has an algebraic complement inside $T^R_zO$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_compl_le_of_sup_eq⟧, and §V.16 gives good position.

**Openness** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_isOpen_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧. Let $X$ be tame, $f$ with tame germ data, $(f, x_0)$ in general position. By Lemma 5.26 it is in good position; the previous paragraph turns its general position into general position of the submanifold $S_f \cap V$ at $x_0$; Theorem 4.22 (3) for tame $X$ (Part IV) makes that open along the submanifold ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_4_22⟧; Definition 4.21 depends only on the germ of the submanifold, since tangent spaces of chart models agree on open sets ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.congr_nhds⟧; and the equivalence turns it back into general position of $(f, y)$ at the nearby zeros. The text uses this without proof ("they will also hold at $(0, y)$ for $y \in S_f$ close to $x$"; "the properties (i)–(ii) hold for all $(\lambda, y) \in \tilde S$").

### V.19 Properties (i)–(ii)

In a chart centred at $y$, with a presentation $T$, the properties of the proof of Theorem 5.18 are ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP⟧: (i) $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)(T_0O) + \operatorname{span}\{\hat t_i(0)\} = K_0$ — $F'(0, y)$ onto; (ii) every $w \in T_0O$ is $u + e$ with $e \in E_0$ and $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)u + \sum a_i\hat t_i(0) = 0$ for some $a$ — $\ker F'(0, y)$ transversal to $\mathbb R^m \oplus T^R$. Adding sections keeps both, by linear algebra ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP.comp⟧.

**(i)–(ii) give general position** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP⟧. In the tame product chart $(r \mapsto r) \times \Phi$ of a tame chart centred at $y$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · pc0⟧, whose tangent space at the centre is $\mathbb R^m \times T_0O$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · ofProd_mem_rangeS⟧ and whose reduced tangent space is $\mathbb R^m \times T^R_0O$, the minimal subspace of $\mathbb R^m$ being everything ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · minimalSubspaceWith_rnPres⟧: (i) is the surjectivity of $F'(0, y)$; (ii) says $\ker F'(0, y) + T^R = T(\mathbb R^m \times O)$ on level $0$, so the kernel has an algebraic complement inside $T^R$, and §V.16 gives good position of $(F, (0, y))$. *Then* $\ker F'(0, y) = T_{(0, y)}\tilde S$ (§V.17), which is finite-dimensional and smooth; a finite-dimensional smooth subspace has an sc-complement inside any sc-subspace it complements algebraically ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · exists_scComplement_le⟧, which gives Definition 5.17 for $F$. The text's "at this point the combined system of sections already satisfies (i) and (ii)" compresses these two steps.

**General position gives (i)–(ii)** in every tame chart centred at $y$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isParamGP_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧: (i) is surjectivity read in the product chart; for (ii), $\tilde S$ is in general position at $(0, y)$ (§V.18), and in the product chart its tangent space is $\ker F'(0, y)$, which therefore has a complement inside $\mathbb R^m \times T^R$.

**Achieving (i)–(ii)** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_sections_isParamGP⟧. Spanning sections give (i) (§V.12) ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · spanning_of_isLinSurjAt⟧. For (ii), "take a linear subspace $L$ complementing $T^R_xX$ in $T_xX$ and add sections which at $x$ span $f'(x)L$": the sections must come from Lemma 5.11, which needs *smooth* points of the fibre, so $L$ must consist of smooth vectors. The coordinates $\lambda_{I(0)}$ map $T_0O$ onto $\mathbb R^{I(0)}$ with kernel $T^R_0O$ (Proposition 2.36), and already map the dense smooth vectors of $T_0O$ onto it (a dense subspace of a finite-dimensional image is all of it); so there are smooth $l_i \in T_0O$ with $\lambda(l_i) = e_i$. $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)l_i$ is smooth ($\mathrm{Lin}$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point), Lemma 5.11 gives allowable sections through $\Phi^{-1}(0, \mathrm{Lin}_g(0)l_i)$ supported in $U$, and with these added every $w \in T_0O$ is $u + e$: subtract $\sum\lambda_i(w)l_i$, whose image under $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)$ is cancelled by the new sections.

### V.20 Theorem 5.18

**From a family** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_18_of_family⟧. Let $X$ be tame, $f$ with tame germ data and compact solution set, $N$ auxiliary, $U$ from Theorem 5.5. Fix $s_0$ with $\operatorname{supp}s_0 \subseteq U$, $N(s_0) \le 1 - \varepsilon$, and allowable $t_1, \dots, t_m$ with $F$ in general position at every $(0, x)$, $x \in S_g$, $g = f + s_0$.

1. *General position near the zero slice.* $\mathbb R^m \times X$ is tame ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · prod_rn_isTame⟧ and $F$ has tame germ data ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbationG · theorem_3_18_tame⟧, so openness (§V.18) gives, around each $(0, x)$, an open set on which the zeros of $F$ are in good and general position; their union $W \supseteq \{0\} \times S_g$.
2. *Compactness and the omitted step* as in §V.13: the zeros $Z$ of $F$ over $|\lambda| \le \delta_1$ are compact, and $Z \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta_0\} \subseteq W$.
3. *The submanifold.* $A = \tilde S \cap W \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta\}$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb R^m \times X$ (the bridge lemma, §V.17), in general position at each of its points (Definition 4.21, by §V.18 and locality), with compact closure (inside $Z$).
4. *Theorem 4.23.* In its countable-cover form (Part IV) ⟦Chapter4/Families · theorem_4_23_of_subset⟧, it gives a set $\Sigma$ of parameters with null complement over which the fibre $A_\lambda$ is a smooth submanifold of $X$ in general position.
5. *Transversality.* The Sard step of §V.14 on the compact zeros over $|\lambda| \le \delta/2$ gives a further null set off which the slices are transversal at their zeros.
6. *The conclusions for $\lambda$.* For $|\lambda| < \delta/2$ off both null sets, with $h = f + s_\lambda$: the fibre of $A$ over $\lambda$ is $S_h$; $h$ is transversal; $S_h$ is a submanifold in general position, so $(h, y)$ is in good position (§V.18), and then in general position by the equivalence of §V.18 applied at $y$ together with the locality of Definition 4.21; Theorem 4.18 gives the corner structure and tameness of $S_h$ ⟦Chapter4/Submanifolds · MPolyfold.theorem_4_18⟧, and Theorem 4.22 (2) gives $d_{S_h} = d_X$ on $S_h$ ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_4_22⟧. These are the conclusions collected in ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundle.SolutionSetInGeneralPosition⟧.

**The generic form** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_18⟧. At every zero $x$ of $g$ choose a tame chart centred at $x$ with a presentation; sections with (i)–(ii) there (§V.19) make $F_x$ general at $(0, x)$, hence (openness, §V.18) at $(0, y)$ for the zeros $y$ in an open $U(x)$. Finitely many $U(x_j)$ cover $S_g$; the united family $t$ keeps (i)–(ii) at every $(0, y)$ — read (i)–(ii) off general position in the chart of $x_j$, add sections, go back — so $F$ is in general position at every $(0, y)$, and the previous theorem applies. "Replacing $f + s_0$ by $f$ and $N$ by $cN$" is not needed; the proof keeps $s_0$.

**The dense form** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_18_dense⟧ is derived exactly as for Theorem 5.13 (§V.15).

The text's $\tilde S$ omits the equation $F = 0$, and its "$p^{-1}(\{|\lambda| \le \varepsilon\})$ is compact" is the omitted step of §V.13.

### V.21 Theorem 5.25

⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_25⟧. Let $X$ be tame with bump functions, $f$ proper with tame germ data. Properness gives a compact solution set; Theorem 5.18 with $s_0 = 0$ gives $U$, $t$, $\delta$ and a null $CV$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.fiberZero_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · sectionAdd_fiberZero⟧; the ball $\{|\lambda| < \delta\}$ has positive measure, so some $\lambda$ avoids $CV$, and $s = \sum\lambda_it_i$ is allowable with $f + s$ in general position at every zero and all the conclusions of Theorem 5.18; Lemma 5.26 turns general into good position in the tame chart of the germ data (§V.16). The text's proof says "in view of Theorem 3.54 ... in general position", which is the openness of §V.18 (Theorem 3.54 is about good position), and writes $x \in S_f$ for $x \in S_{f+s_0}$. Here $U$ is the neighbourhood Theorem 5.18 produces; the text lets the reader choose "an associated" one.

### V.22 Theorem 5.19

⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_19⟧. Let $X$ admit bump functions, $f$ have tame germ data and compact solution set, and $(f, x)$ be in good position at the zeros $x \in \partial X$. The text's "as before" applies the implicit function theorem to $F$ at the boundary zeros $(0, x)$, where all $t_i$ vanish and $\ker F'(0, x) = \mathbb R^m \times \ker f'(x)$; this is in good position to $\mathbb R^m \times C_x$ only if $\ker f'(x) + E_x \supseteq T_xX$, a general position condition that good position does not imply ($\mathbb R(1, 1)$ in $[0, \infty)^2$; checked on paper only). The formal proof avoids those points:

1. *Near the boundary zeros.* Theorem 3.54 (1) at each zero of $f$ on $\partial X$ gives an open set of zeros in good position ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoG · theorem_3_54_one'⟧; their union $V_{bd}$, and an open $V_1$ with $S_f \cap \partial X \subseteq V_1$ and $\operatorname{cl}V_1 \subseteq V_{bd}$.
2. *Away from them.* The zeros of $f$ outside $V_1$ are not on $\partial X$, so interior ($d = 0$). Spanning sections at these zeros are taken with supports in $U \setminus (\partial X \cup \operatorname{cl}V_1)$, an open set containing them; finitely many families cover the compact $S_f \setminus V_1$, and $F$ is onto at every $(0, y)$, $y \in S_f$ outside $V_1$.
3. *Good position of $F$ off the boundary.* At the interior points good position is surjectivity ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexG · StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt⟧; Theorem 3.54 (1) for $F$ gives an open $W \supseteq \{0\} \times (S_f \setminus V_1)$ of zeros in good position, off $\mathbb R^m \times \partial X$.
4. *Compactness and Sard* as in §V.15 for the zeros of $F$ over small $\lambda$ outside $\mathbb R^m \times V_1$.
5. *The conclusions.* For small $\lambda$ off the null set, $h = f + s_\lambda$. On $V_1$ all $t_i$ vanish, so $h = f$ there, and the good position of $(f, y)$ at the zeros in $V_1$ passes to $(h, y)$ because good position depends only on the germ of the section ⟦Chapter3/Chapter5BridgeG · StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.congr_nhds⟧. Off $V_1$ the zeros of $h$ are interior, $h$ is transversal there by the Sard step, hence in good position. Theorem 3.57 makes $S_h$, if non-empty, a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and a manifold with boundary with corners ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsG · theorem_3_57⟧.

$s_\lambda = \sum\lambda_it_i$ has support disjoint from $\partial X$, so it vanishes on the open neighbourhood $X \setminus \operatorname{supp}s_\lambda$ of $\partial X$, and it is "arbitrarily small" as $\lambda \to 0$. The text's tameness of $X$ is not used, and its "$(f, x)$ in good position for every $x \in S_{f+s}$" is $(f + s, x)$. No dense form is stated.

### V.23 Definition 5.20, and Lemmas 5.23 and 5.24

**Definition 5.20** ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy⟧. $X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data and compact solution set, $t : X \to \mathbb R$ sc-smooth with $t(X) = [0, 1]$, and for every $\tau \in [0, 1]$: $X_\tau = t^{-1}(\tau)$ a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.19) with tame induced structure, on which the restriction $f|X_\tau$ — the section $a \mapsto (a, f(a))$ of the pull-back of $P$ along the inclusion ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · restrictSection⟧ ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · StrongBundle.pullback⟧, the inclusion being sc-smooth (Proposition 2.21) — has tame germ data. The text never says what $Y|X_t$ is; the pull-back of Proposition 2.54 is the strong bundle structure available. The end problems are the restrictions to $t^{-1}(0)$ and $t^{-1}(1)$; their solution sets are $S_f \cap X_\tau$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · isZeroAt_restrictSection_iff⟧, closed in the compact $S_f$, hence compact ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict⟧.

**Lemma 5.23 and the hidden hypothesis.** The proof of Theorem 5.22 fixes a critical point $x$ of $t|S$ and says "since $x$ is a smooth point, we find a one-dimensional smooth linear sc-subspace $Z \subset T_xX$ such that $T_xX = Z \oplus \ker(dt(x))$". For $dt(x) = 0$, $\ker dt(x) = T_xX$ and the only complement is $0$: a non-zero complement exists only if $\ell \ne 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · ne_zero_of_isCompl_ker⟧. Theorem 5.22 does not assume that $t$ is a submersion at the critical points of $t|S$, so this is a hidden hypothesis. When $\ell \ne 0$, some vector $e$ of any spanning set (e.g. the dense smooth vectors) has $\ell(e) \ne 0$, and $\mathbb Re$ complements $\ker\ell$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · exists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero⟧. Lemma 5.23 is then linear algebra: $\ell|_Z$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathbb R$, so $b = (\ell|_Z)^{-1} \circ \tau$ is the unique $b : S \to Z$ with $\ell \circ b = \tau$, and adding $a$ with values in $\ker\ell$ does not change $\ell \circ b$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · lemma_5_23⟧.

**The calculus.** At a level-$1$ point $z$, $D(a \cdot w)(z)v = Da(z)v \cdot w(z) + a(z)Dw(z)v$ for sc-smooth $a : U \to \mathbb R$, $w : U \to F$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · scDeriv_smul_apply⟧, and $D(\ell(\rho(\cdot) - p))(z) = \ell \circ D\rho(z)$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · scDeriv_clm_sub_apply⟧. The function $g = \beta \cdot \ell(\varphi(\cdot) - \varphi(x))$ on $\operatorname{dom}\varphi$, $0$ outside ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · chartLinCutoff⟧, is sc-smooth when $\beta$ is with $\operatorname{supp}\beta \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · isScSmoothMap_chartLinCutoff⟧.

**Lemma 5.24.** *The construction* ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · exists_scPlusSection_linAt⟧: for a chart $\Phi$ around the smooth point $x$, a smooth point $e$ over $x$, a continuous linear $\ell$ on the model space and $U \ni x$, let $s_e$ be the sc⁺-section through $e$ of Lemma 5.11, supported in $U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$, $\beta$ a bump with $\beta \equiv 1$ near $x$ and support in the chart domain, and $s = g \cdot s_e$ with $g$ as above. Then $s$ is sc⁺ (§V.9), $s(x) = g(x)e = 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · principal_sectionSmul⟧, $\operatorname{supp}s \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · sectionSupport_sectionSmul_subset⟧, and in the chart, by the product rule, $\mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = D(g \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(z)v \cdot \hat s_e(\varphi(x)) + g(x)\mathrm{Lin}_{s_e}(z)v = \ell(Dr(z)v)\Phi(e)_2 = \ell(v)\Phi(e)_2$ for $v \in T_zO$, since $g \circ \varphi^{-1} = \ell(\cdot - \varphi(x))$ near $\varphi(x)$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · chartLinCutoff_of_mem⟧ and $Dr(z) = 1$ on $T_zO$. *The lemma* ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · lemma_5_24⟧: for a finite-dimensional $K \subseteq T_zO$ (the text's $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$) and a linear $b : K \to T_zO$ with $\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2$, extend $-\lambda$ (linear on the finite-dimensional $K$) to a continuous linear functional $\ell$ on the model space (Hahn–Banach) and apply the construction: $\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) + \mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 - \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 = 0$. The text's graph of $S$ over $T_xS$, its complement $L$ with $j : L \to \mathbb R$, and its case "if this operator is the zero operator we can take $s = 0$" are not needed. That $f'(x) \circ b_\tau$ has its image in the line of a *smooth* point is a hypothesis; the text's justification ("the image of any vector in $T_xS$ belongs to $Y_\infty$") is not formalized.

### V.24 Bump functions in local models: Theorem 5.34 and Proposition 5.35

**Definition 5.33** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · LocalModel.HasBumpProperty⟧. For $x \in O$ and $W$ open in $E_0$ with $\operatorname{cl}(O \cap W) \subseteq O$, an sc-smooth $f$ on $O$ with $f(x) \ne 0$ (as in Definition 5.9) and support in $O$ inside $W$.

**A retract is closed near its points** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · closure_inter_ball_subset⟧. If $B(z, r) \subseteq W'$ and $U = C \cap W'$ is the domain of a retraction $\rho$ onto $O$, then $O \cap \operatorname{cl}B(z, r/2) \subseteq O$: a limit of points of $O$ in the closed half ball lies in $C$ ($C$ closed) and in $B(z, r)$, hence in $U$, where $\rho$ is continuous, and it is a fixed point of $\rho$.

**Theorem 5.34** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · theorem_5_34⟧. "⇒": every chart's model has the property — given $x$, $W$, a bump of $X$ at $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ supported in $\varphi^{-1}(O \cap W)$, read in the chart. "⇐", "clearly" in the text, hides a support condition: a local bump $f_0$ with support in $U(x)$, $\operatorname{cl}_E(U(x)) \subseteq O$, gives $f = f_0 \circ \varphi$ on the chart domain, but $\operatorname{cl}_X\{f \ne 0\}$ may leave the domain. For $X = E$ a Hilbert space, the chart $\varphi(u) = u/(1 - |u|_0^2)$ from the open unit ball onto $O = E$, $U(x) = O$ and $f_0 \equiv 1$, the extension by $0$ is the indicator of the ball. The proof chooses $U_1 \ni x$ with $\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ (regularity of $X$) and $r$ with $B(\varphi(x), r) \cap O \subseteq \varphi(U_1)$, takes the local bump in $W = B(\varphi(x), r/2)$ — admissible by the previous paragraph — and extends $f_0 \circ \varphi$ by $0$: its support lies in $\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U$, and it is sc-smooth because it vanishes on the open complement of its support and is sc-smooth in the chart (§V.8).

**Proposition 5.35.** If $\kappa\|v\|^2 \le b(v, v)$ for a continuous bilinear $b$ on $E_0$, then $f(v) = \tau(1 - b(v - x, v - x)/\rho)$ is $C^\infty$ on $E_0$, equal to $1$ at $x$ and supported in a small ball; it is sc-smooth on $E$ by Corollary 1.20 from the base level ⟦Chapter1/Levels · IsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional⟧, and so is its composition with any retraction onto $O$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic⟧. "$E_0$ is a Hilbert space" is stated as $\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · proposition_5_35⟧: an inner product structure on $E_0$ would be a second normed structure next to that of the sc-scale. Translating by a non-smooth $x$ is legitimate here because $f$ is $C^\infty$ on $E_0$ itself; for a merely sc-smooth function it would not be. With Theorem 5.34: an M-polyfold covered by charts on sc-Hilbert spaces admits sc-smooth bump functions, the remark before Definition 5.9 ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert⟧.

### V.25 Partitions of unity: Theorem 5.37 and Proposition 5.38

**The algebra of sc-smooth functions.** Sums, differences and products of sc-smooth functions are sc-smooth, on retracts ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsScSmoothRetractMap.real_add⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsScSmoothRetractMap.real_mul⟧ and on $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_add⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_sub⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_mul⟧, and so are finite sums and products ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsetSum⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsetProd⟧. Sc-smoothness is local ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_eventuallyEq⟧, so a locally finite sum, which near each point is a finite sum, is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsum⟧; and a function supported in a chart domain with sc-smooth representative is sc-smooth on $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_chart⟧.

**Definitions 5.28 and 5.36.** A partition of unity is Mathlib's (continuous $\rho_i \ge 0$, locally finite supports, $\sum\rho_i = 1$), sc-smooth if every $\rho_i$ is ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity⟧; $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate one ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧. The approximation property: for $V = O \cap W$ with $\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O$, continuous $f : O \to [0, 1]$ supported in $V$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, an sc-smooth $g : O \to [0, 1]$ supported in $V$ with $|f - g| \le \varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · LocalModel.HasApproxProperty⟧. Partitions of unity give bump functions: the function attached to $U$ of a partition subordinate to $\{U, X \setminus \{x\}\}$ is $1$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity.admitsBumpFunctions⟧ — the easy half of the open problem the text states after Definition 5.29.

**"(i) ⇒ (ii)"** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · hasApproxProperty_restrict⟧. The text calls $f \circ \varphi$ "sc-smooth" ($f$ is only continuous) and asserts $\operatorname{cl}_X(\varphi^{-1}(V)) \subseteq U$; with the chart of the unit ball above, $V = O$ and $f \equiv 1$, the extension by $0$ is not continuous. Since (ii) asks only for *some* atlas, the proof restricts each chart to an open $s$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X(s) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$. Then for closed $A \subseteq \varphi(s)$ the set $\varphi^{-1}(A)$ is closed in $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MChart.isClosed_inter_preimage⟧, so $F = f \circ \varphi$ extended by $0$ is continuous. Cover $X$ by $\{F < \varepsilon/2\}$ and the sets $U_x = \{|F - F(x)| < \varepsilon/2\} \cap \varphi^{-1}(V)$, take a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity $(\beta_0, \beta_x)$, and let $\hat g = \sum_x\beta_xF(x)$: a locally finite sum of sc-smooth functions with values in $[0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.finsum_mul_mem_Icc⟧, supported in $\varphi^{-1}(V)$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.tsupport_finsum_mul_subset⟧, and within $\varepsilon/2$ of $F$, since every $F(x)$ with $\beta_x(y) \ne 0$ is ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.abs_sub_finsum_mul_le⟧. Whether *every* chart has the property is not settled.

**"(ii) ⇒ (i)".** Every point of a chart domain has small open neighbourhoods $N$ with $\operatorname{cl}_XN \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{cl}\varphi(N) \subseteq O$ — half a ball inside the domain of a retraction, closed by §V.24 ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MChart.exists_small_nhds⟧ — and the approximation property transports to continuous functions on $X$ supported in such $N$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · LocalModel.HasApproxProperty.exists_approx⟧. *Sc-smooth Urysohn functions* ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · exists_isScSmoothMap_urysohn⟧: for disjoint closed $s, t$, cover $t$ by small neighbourhoods $W_x$ inside $X \setminus s$, take continuous $f_x = 1$ near $x$ supported in $W_x$, a locally finite refinement, approximations $\hat g_x$ within $1/2$ — so $\hat g_x \ge 1/2$ where $f_x = 1$ — and $F = \tau(4\sum\hat g_x - 1)$, sc-smooth, $0$ on $s$ and $1$ on $t$. Then Mathlib's bump coverings produce a covering indexed by the given cover with sc-smooth functions ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_prop⟧, and $\rho_i = f_i\prod_{j < i}(1 - f_j)$, locally a finite product, is the partition of unity ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx⟧. This replaces the text's refinement "with the same index set", which does not exist in general (the cover $\{X\}$); metrizability is not needed.

**Theorem 5.37** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · theorem_5_37⟧ combines the two directions, "atlas" read as a family of charts covering $X$.

**Proposition 5.38** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_38⟧ is not "an immediate consequence of Theorem 5.37": that theorem produces some atlas, not the given model, and applied to $O$ would need partitions of unity on an open subset of $C$. The proof repeats "(i) ⇒ (ii)" in $E_0$: $A = \{x \in O \mid f(x) \ge \varepsilon/2\}$ is closed in $E_0$ because $\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O$; $E_0 \setminus A$ and balls $B(x, r_x) \subseteq W$, $x \in V$, on which $f$ varies by less than $\varepsilon/2$, cover $E_0$; a $C^\infty$ partition of unity of $E_0$ gives $g = \sum\beta_xf(x)$, $C^\infty$ on $E_0$, hence sc-smooth (Corollary 1.20), composed with a retraction onto $O$.

### V.26 Banach space geometry: Definitions 5.31, 5.39, 5.41, Proposition 5.42, Corollary 5.44

A Banach space admits a $C^k$-bump function if some $C^k$ function, not identically zero, has bounded support ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · HasContDiffBump⟧, and $C^k$ partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate $C^k$ one ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · AdmitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity⟧. $c_0(\Gamma)$ is the subspace of $\ell^\infty(\Gamma)$ of functions tending to $0$ along the cofinite filter ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · cZero⟧, equivalently with $\{|f(\gamma)| > \varepsilon\}$ finite for every $\varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · mem_cZero_iff⟧, normed by the supremum ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · norm_cZero⟧; coordinate-wise $C^k$ embeddings are as in the text ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsCoordinatewiseContDiffEmbedding⟧, and Toruńczyk's Theorem 5.40 is recorded as a statement, not proved and not used ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · TorunczykStatement⟧. WCG means a weakly compact set with dense span ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsWCG⟧; reflexive, used in Proposition 5.42 and not defined in the text, means $V \to V''$ onto ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsReflexive⟧.

**Proposition 5.42.** (i) For reflexive $V$ the weak closure of the closed unit ball is weakly compact — Kakutani's theorem, in Mathlib as Banach–Alaoglu in $V''$ through the embedding of $(V, \text{weak})$ into $(V'', \text{weak-*})$ ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/DoubleDual · NormedSpace.isCompact_closure_of_isBounded⟧ — and its span contains the ball, hence is $V$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · span_closedBall_eq_top⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_42_reflexive⟧. (ii) For separable $V$, a dense sequence $(y_n)$ scaled by $1/((n + 1)(|y_n| + 1))$ is a null sequence; with $0$ it is norm compact, hence weakly compact, and its span contains every $y_n$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_42_separable⟧. The text's "$\{0\} \cup \{x_n/n\}$" has its index range missing.

**Corollary 5.44** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · corollary_5_44⟧. Let $\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)$ on $E_0$, and assume Theorem 5.43 for $E_0$ and $k = \infty$, recorded as a statement ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement⟧. A Hilbert space is reflexive: the parallelogram law holds, so the norm comes from an inner product ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/OfNorm · InnerProductSpace.ofNorm⟧, and every $\phi \in V''$ is evaluation at the Riesz representative of $x \mapsto \phi(\langle x, \cdot\rangle)$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isReflexive_of_hilbert⟧; hence WCG by Proposition 5.42 (i). It has the $C^\infty$-bump $\tau(1 - b(v, v))$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · hasContDiffBump_of_hilbert⟧. Theorem 5.43 gives $C^\infty$ partitions of unity of $E_0$, and Proposition 5.38 — not Theorem 5.37, as the text says — the approximation property. With Theorem 5.37, an M-polyfold on such charts admits sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert⟧.

### V.27 What is not formalized

- **Corollary 5.8 as one statement for all $i$.** It is proved for each fixed $i$ (§V.29; gap G.41 closed in the fourth addendum). Not formalized: a family $P^i$ indexed by $i$, the identification of the iterated base $(X^1)^1$ with $X_2$ as a topological space (the sets agree; gap G.6), and the tame form of the conclusion, which needs the tameness of the index raises of tame charts. Condition (3) of a filling on level $1$ does not follow from level $0$ alone — on $E_m = \{x \mid \sum e^{2mk}x_k^2 < \infty\}$ the right shift $T$ makes $1 - T/2$ invertible on $E_0$ while $(1 - T/2)^{-1}e_0 = \sum2^{-n}e_n \notin E_1$ — so the corollary's proof needs the regularity argument of §V.29, through Lemma 3.17 ⟦Chapter3/Filler · lemma_3_17⟧.
- **The non-completeness of $(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ in the text's setting** (§V.30), and the identification of the completion of Remark 5.12; **Remarks 5.14, 5.16, 5.21** (gaps G.43, G.44, G.47), and **a dense form of Theorem 5.19** (gap G.45).
- **Weak against pointwise bump functions at a non-smooth point** (§V.31).
- **Finding 88** (gap G.46): the failure of good position of $F$ at the boundary zeros (§V.22) is checked on paper only.
- **Theorem 5.22** (gap G.48): it needs finite-dimensional Morse theory on manifolds with boundary, the cotangent bundle of the solution set, a parametric Sard theorem and a trivialization of the family $S_\lambda$, none in Mathlib or the project, and the hidden hypothesis $dt(x) \ne 0$ (§V.23). **Theorem 5.27** (gap G.49): "the proof is left to the reader".
- **Theorems 5.32, 5.40, 5.43 and the Sobolev remark** (gaps G.50–G.53): deep Banach space geometry cited from [9], [12], and Sobolev spaces with their sc-structures (gap G.1). Nothing on the main line uses partitions of unity.

### V.28 What the formalization taught us

**The tameness hypothesis.** The first formal versions of Theorem 5.13 and Lemma 5.26 assumed, as the §3.6 theorems then did, that the base retraction of *every* compatible strong bundle chart — and of every chart of the pull-backs to $\mathbb R^k \times X$ — is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies this (a compatible chart $(1, \varphi)$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ is never tame), so those statements were vacuous. The repair is the text's own Definitions 3.50, 3.51, 3.53 in a tame chart: the perturbation theorems take $f$ with tame germ data, the parametrized sections inherit them through the tame product chart, and Definition 5.17 lives in a tame chart, where Lemma 5.26's count $\dim T_zO/T^R_zO = d_C(z)$ holds.

**What "it is easily verified" costs.** The perturbation theorems of §5.3 are sketches. Their formal proofs needed the density of smooth vectors (§V.12), the compactness of the zeros over a small parameter ball (§V.13), a local, stratified Sard step (§V.14), the bridge from tangent germ data to Definition 4.13 (§V.17), $T_yS = \ker f'(y)$ by a dimension count, which gives the chart independence of Definition 5.17 and the openness of general position (§§V.17–V.18), and, in Theorem 5.19, a route around the implicit function theorem at boundary points where its hypothesis fails (§V.22).

### V.29 Corollary 5.8 on the shifted strong bundle

Corollary 5.8 says that, for an sc-Fredholm section $f$ with compact solution set, $f^i$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^i : Y^i \to X^i$ with compact solution set, and that "it is a priori clear that $f^i$ is sc-Fredholm". The text defines $Y[i]$ for $i = 0, 1$ only, never $Y^i$, and "a priori clear" hides the filler condition on level $1$ (§V.7). Both are supplied here (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140–146).

**The reading of $Y^1$.** $Y^1 = Y_{1,1}$ with $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$ — the convention of $E^1$ and of $(U \triangleleft F)^1 = U^1 \triangleleft F^1$ — not $Y[1] = Y_{0,1}$ and not $Y_{1,2}$. It is forced by "$f^i$ is obtained by raising the index": an sc-smooth section maps $X_1$ into $Y_{1,1}$, and in general not into $Y_{1,2}$.

**Fibres of a strong bundle.** Through a chart, $P^{-1}(x)$ is linearly homeomorphic to $K_{\varphi(x)} = \{h \mid \Gamma(\varphi(x), h) = h\}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.fiberK⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.fiberCLE⟧, the fixed points of a continuous projection, a closed subspace of the fibre model ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.isClosed_fiberK⟧; so every fibre is a Banach space ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.isBanachable_fiber⟧, which Definition 2.51 asks of a strong bundle.

**The levels of $X^1$, and raising the index of maps.** $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ and $(X^1)_\infty = X_\infty$ as sets ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.mem_shift_smoothSet_iff⟧ (their topologies are not compared; gap G.6). An sc-smooth map $f : X \to Z$ between M-polyfolds induces an sc-smooth $f_1 : X^1 \to Z^1$: continuity, and in the level charts the local representatives are the level-$1$ maps of those of $f$, sc-smooth by Proposition 1.17 for retracts ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.levelChart_apply_levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne⟧.

**The shifted strong bundle** ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shift⟧. Its total space is $Y_{1,1}$, the level $1$ of the M-polyfold $Y[0]$ with its level topology, Hausdorff and paracompact by Theorem 2.16 ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.ShiftSpace⟧; the projection is $P^1 = P|_{Y_{1,1}}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftProj⟧, continuous and onto ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.continuous_shiftProj⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.surjective_shiftProj⟧; the fibre $P^{-1}(x) \cap Y_{1,1}$ is a linear subspace — in a chart it is the preimage of $F_1$ under the linear fibre map ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftFiberSubmodule⟧ — carries the topology of $F_1$, not that of $P^{-1}(x)$, and is a Banach space, a closed subspace of $F_1$ through a chart ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.banachable_shift⟧. The atlas consists of the *index raises* of the strong bundle charts ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftAtlas⟧: base chart the level chart $\varphi^1 : V_1 \to O_1$, fibre model $F^1$, retraction $R$ on $U^1 \triangleleft F^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · IsStrongBundleRetraction.shift⟧, bundle chart the level chart of $\Phi$ in $Y[0]$. Compatible charts have compatible index raises ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.shift⟧: on $[0]$ the transitions are level charts of compatible charts, on $[1]$ the transition $(\Phi'^1 \circ (\Phi^1)^{-1})[1]$ is the level-$1$ map of $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ (Proposition 1.17 for retracts) ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift_transition_one⟧, and the $F_1$-condition of Definition 2.50 holds because the $[1]$-transition is sc⁰ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift_compatible_range⟧. Checks: $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.mem_shift_doubleLevel_iff⟧, the M-polyfold $Y^1[0]$ is $Y[0]^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isChart_shift_toMPolyfold0_iff⟧, and the index raise of every chart of $P$ is a chart of $P^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isChart_shift⟧.

**The section $f^1$.** $f^1 = f|_{X_1}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.sectionShift⟧ is a section of $P^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isSection_sectionShift⟧, sc-smooth by the raising of the index of maps ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.shift⟧, with the zeros of $f$ in $X_1$ as its zeros ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.solutionSet_sectionShift⟧, and regularizing, from $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ and $(Y^1)_{m,m+1} = Y_{m+1,m+2}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.regularizing_sectionShift⟧. In the index raise of a chart the principal part of $f^1$ is the level-$1$ map of that of $f$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.principal_sectionShift⟧, and the raised chart is centred where the chart is ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_φ_eq_zero⟧.

**Condition (3) on every level, at every centre** ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_fillDefect⟧. *Let $(g, s)$ be a datum of Definition 3.11 in a chart — $g$ a filling germ of $\hat f$ with fill defect $k = [1 - \rho(r)]g$ and derivative family $Dk$, $s$ an sc⁺-germ with $s(0) = g(0)$, $g - s$ conjugated to a basic germ. If $v \in \ker Dr(0)$ and $Dk(0)v \in F_m$, then $v \in E_m$* — at the centre of the datum, which need not be a zero. At a zero this is the regularity of §III.45 ⟦Chapter3/LinearizationChartsScG · IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_scDeriv_r_eq_zero⟧. The reduction to a zero needs neither a global sc⁺-section nor a bump function: $g(0) = \iota s(0)$ is a smooth point of $F$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsScSmoothGerm.toBase_zero_mem_smooth⟧; $\hat s(z) = \Gamma(z, -g(0))$ is sc-smooth on $U$ ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoXi · isScSmooth_const_of_smooth⟧ and a section of $K \to O$, so by Lemma 3.17 $g' = g + \hat s \circ r$ fills $\hat f + \hat s$ with the *same* fill defect ⟦Chapter3/GermCalculus · IsFillingGerm.add_section⟧, and $g'(0) = g(0) - \Gamma(0, g(0)) = 0$. With the sc⁺-germ $s' = s + \Gamma^1(r(\cdot), -s(0))$, $g' - s' = g - s$ on $U$, so Proposition 3.52 in sc form makes $Dg'(0)$ sc-Fredholm ⟦Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationScG · proposition_3_52_local_sc⟧; and $Dk(0) = (1 - \rho(0))Dg'(0)$ ⟦Chapter3/GermFillerLinearization · fillDefect_deriv_zero_eq_rho⟧, so the case of a zero applies to $g'$.

**The filling on level $1$** ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsFillingGerm.germ_shift⟧. The fill defect of $g^1$ is the level-$1$ map of $k$, an sc¹-germ with derivative family $(Dk)_1$ by Proposition 1.17 for germs ⟦Chapter3/GermLevels · IsSc1GermWith.shift⟧; $\iota\,Dr^1(0) = Dr(0)\,\iota$, by the uniqueness of the derivative of $r^1 = r_1$ on the shifted germ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · toBase_scDeriv_r_shift⟧, and $\iota\,\rho^1(0) = \rho(0)\,\iota$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · toBase_ρCLM_shift⟧. So $Dk^1(0) = Dk(0)|_{E_1}$ maps $\ker Dr^1(0)$ to $\ker\rho^1(0)$; it is injective by condition (3) on level $0$, onto by the regularity just proved with $m = 1$, and a topological isomorphism by the open mapping theorem. Conditions (1) and (2) of the filling shift directly ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_eq_on⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_mem_of_fixed⟧, and $g^1$ is a filling germ of the principal part of $f^1$ in $\Phi^1$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_isFillingGerm⟧.

**Corollary 5.8.** At every smooth point of $X^1$, the datum $(g, s)$ of $f$ in a chart $\Phi$ gives the datum $(g^1, s^1)$ of $f^1$ in $\Phi^1$: $g^1$ fills, $s^1$ is an sc⁺-germ on the shifted germ, $s^1(0) = g^1(0)$, and $g^1 - s^1 = (g - s)_1$ near $0$ is conjugated to a basic germ by the index raise of the conjugation (§V.7) ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · isScFredholmGerm_sectionShift⟧. *For an sc-Fredholm section $f$, $f^1$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^1$* ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_8_isScFredholmSection⟧; *if $f$ has compact solution set, so has $f^1$*, by the compactness on level $1$ (§V.7) ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_8⟧. Since this holds for every strong bundle, it applies to $P^1$ and $f^1$: $f^2 = (f^1)^1$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^2 = (P^1)^1$ with compact solution set ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_8_two⟧, and so on for every fixed $i$. The unpacked data in the shifted chart are kept for reference ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_8_data⟧. No hypothesis beyond the text's is added, and tameness is not used. *Not done*: a family $P^i$ indexed by $i$ (a dependent type of strong bundles), the identification of $(X^1)^1$ with $X_2$ as topological spaces, and the tame form of the conclusion — germ data of $f^1$ in tame charts of $P^1$ — which needs the presentation independence of the degeneracy index for $C^1$ and that $A \cap E_1$ is an sc-complement of $T_xO^1$ when $A$ is one of $T_xO$; there is no counterexample either.

### V.30 The metric $\rho$ on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$

The text: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ "becomes a metric space" for $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, and "is not complete" (p. 174). The first is proved here; the second turns out to need a hypothesis (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153).

**The metric.** $\rho(s, s')$ is the supremum of the pointwise distances of §V.10 ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist⟧. For an auxiliary norm the fibre norm is symmetric and subadditive (Definition 5.1 (1)) ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.neg⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_le⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_triangle⟧, so for allowable sections $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le N(s(x)) + N(s'(x)) \le 2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.sectionDistAt_le_two⟧: the supremum is finite and $\rho \le 2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_le_two⟧. $\rho(s, s) = 0$, symmetry and the triangle inequality come from the fibre norms ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_self⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_comm⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_triangle⟧, and $\rho(s, s') = 0$ forces $s = s'$ because $N$ vanishes only at $0_x$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.eq_of_allowableDist_eq_zero⟧. So $\rho$ is a metric ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableMetric⟧, carried by a type synonym of $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, since the sections $X \to Y$ carry the product topology ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.AllowableSpace⟧. Only Definition 5.1 (1) is used. The density statements of Theorems 5.13 and 5.18 (§§V.15, V.20) are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_le_iff⟧.

**Not complete, by an example** ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections⟧. Take the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ of the non-vacuity witnesses of Chapter 3, the fibre norm $N(x, v) = |v|$ — an auxiliary norm, including the condition on the topology of $Y[1]$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.fibNorm⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isAuxNorm_fibNorm⟧ — and $U = \mathbb R$. Graphs of $C^\infty$ maps are sc⁺-sections ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_graphSection⟧, so $s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))$ is allowable, with $N \le 1/2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.approx⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.graphSection_approx_mem⟧, and $\rho(s_i, s_j) \le (\varepsilon_i + \varepsilon_j)/2$ with $\varepsilon_j = 1/(j+1)$, by $|\sqrt{x^2 + a^2} - |x|| \le a$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.abs_sqrt_sub_abs_le⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.abs_approx_sub_limitFn⟧. A $\rho$-limit $s$ would have, by pointwise convergence, the fibre part $|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.limitFn⟧, which is not differentiable at $0$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.not_differentiableAt_limit⟧; but the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is $C^1$, by Proposition 1.18 in the chart $\Phi = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.differentiable_snd_of_isScPlusSection⟧.

**Complete, in two cases.** For $U = \emptyset$ every allowable section is the zero section, so the space is a point, for every bundle and auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.subsingleton_allowableSections_empty⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_empty⟧. Over the point $\mathbb R^0$ with fibre $\mathbb R^k$ every section is the graph of a constant, hence sc⁺ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_of_isSection_point⟧, and the space is the closed unit ball of $\mathbb R^k$ (or $\{0\}$), complete for every $U$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point⟧. So the text's "not complete" is false without a hypothesis and is read as "not complete in general". In the text's setting — $U$ a neighbourhood of the solution set of an sc-Fredholm section on an M-polyfold with bump functions — one expects non-completeness as soon as $U$ contains a non-isolated point over which $Y_{0,1}$ is nonzero, by the same mechanism (bump functions times a non-smooth uniform limit); this is not formalized, and neither is the identification of the metric completion with the sections of Remark 5.12 (§V.10).

### V.31 Weak and pointwise bump functions

§V.8 reads Definition 5.9 pointwise, $f(x) \ne 0$, because Proposition 5.30 needs it, and keeps Definition 5.29's "not identically zero" as the weak reading. How far apart are they? (Findings, Chapter 5, items 160–163.)

**Bump points.** $x$ is a *bump point* if every open $U \ni x$ carries an sc-smooth $f$ with $f(x) \ne 0$ and $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.HasBumpAt⟧. The pointwise reading says that every point is a bump point ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_iff_forall_hasBumpAt⟧, and the weak reading holds as soon as the bump points are dense: a bump at a bump point inside $U$ is not identically zero and is supported in $U$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense⟧. (The converse, weak ⟹ dense bump points, is a nested-neighbourhoods argument with Cantor's theorem in a chart; not formalized.)

**On an sc-Banach space.** An sc-Banach space $E$ is an M-polyfold with the identity chart and model $(E, E, E)$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · scChart⟧ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · scPolyfold⟧, whose sc-smooth functions are the sc-smooth maps $E \to \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · isScSmoothMap_scPolyfold_iff⟧. *There the weak reading gives a bump point at every smooth point* ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth⟧: given $x \in E_\infty$ and $B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U$, a weak bump supported in $B(x, \varepsilon/2)$ is non-zero on a non-empty open set, which contains a smooth point $y$ because $E_\infty$ is dense; $a = y - x$ is smooth, so $v \mapsto f(v + a)$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter4/Recentre · isScSmooth_add_const⟧, non-zero at $x$, with support in $B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U$. The argument stops at $E_\infty$: translation by a vector $a \notin E_m$ is not even sc⁰, since it sends $0 \in E_m$ out of $E_m$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · not_isSc0_add_const⟧. On M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert spaces both readings hold at every point ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert⟧. *Open*: whether the weak reading gives a bump function non-zero at a non-smooth point, on an sc-Banach space or an M-polyfold; a counterexample would need an $E_0$ without $C^1$ bump functions.

## Part VI. Linearizations, orientations and invariants (HWZ Chapter 6, §§6.1–6.7)

Chapter 6 builds the orientation theory of sc-Fredholm sections. At a smooth point $x$ it collects the linearizations of $f$ into a convex set $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ of Fredholm operators (§6.1); it fixes the conventions for determinant lines and for the isomorphism attached to a four-term exact sequence (§6.2); it defines the determinant $\det(T) = \lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda^*(\operatorname{coker}T)$ of a Fredholm operator, compares it with the determinants of $PT$ for good left-projections $P$ and of the stabilizations $T_\varphi$, and builds the determinant line bundle $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ over the Fredholm operators (§§6.3–6.4); it then restricts that bundle to $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, propagates its orientations along sc-smooth paths of $X$, first in small neighbourhoods (Theorem 6.35) and then globally, as a functor on the path category (Theorem 6.37), and defines orientability and orientations of $f$, orients the solution set (Theorem 6.41) and the sections $f + s$ over $X \times [0, 1]$ (Remark 6.42) (§6.5); §6.6 states the invariant $\Psi_{(f,o)}$ (Theorem 6.43), and the appendix §6.7 proves Lemma 6.5 and Proposition 6.12. This Part retells §6.1 (§VI.1); §6.2 — determinant lines, Definition 6.3 and Proposition 6.4, the isomorphism $\Phi_E$, Lemma 6.5 and Proposition 6.6 (§§VI.2–VI.3); §6.3 — Definitions 6.7–6.9, Lemma 6.10, the isomorphisms $\gamma^P_T$, the stabilization and the direct sums (§§VI.4–VI.6); §6.4 — the local determinant bundles and $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ (§§VI.7–VI.8); §6.5 — orientations over $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (§VI.9), Proposition 6.28 (§VI.10), Lemmas 6.29–6.31 (§§VI.11–VI.13), the push-forward (§§VI.14–VI.15), Lemma 6.33, Lemma 6.34 and Proposition 6.32 (§§VI.16–VI.17), Theorem 6.35 and Definition 6.36 (§§VI.18–VI.19), the path category (§VI.20), the comparison of charts (§VI.21), the transport and Theorem 6.37 (§§VI.22–VI.23), Definitions 6.38–6.40 (§VI.24), Theorem 6.41 (§VI.25) and Remark 6.42 (§VI.26); §6.6 and Theorem 6.43, which are not formalized (§VI.27); the appendix §6.7 (§§VI.28–VI.29); what is not formalized (§VI.30); and what the formalization taught us (§VI.31). Proposition 6.2 was formalized with Chapter 3 and is retold in §III.49. Each item carries the number of its comparison item (V6.1–V6.64) in `Exposition/verification/ch06.md`.

**What is proved, and what is not.** Theorems 6.35 and 6.37 are proved; so are Propositions 6.4, 6.6, 6.12, 6.15, 6.20, 6.23, 6.24, 6.26, 6.32, Lemmas 6.5, 6.10, 6.11, 6.14, 6.17, 6.18, 6.21, 6.25, 6.31, 6.33, 6.34, Corollary 6.13, Lemma 6.29 in the form the text uses afterwards, the kernel statement of Lemma 6.30, Proposition 6.28 with (1′) in place of (1), the equivalence of Definitions 6.38 and 6.39, Theorem 6.41 in the form of tangent orientations that vary continuously along the paths of zeros in a chart, and Remark 6.42 at a point. Every definition of the chapter is formalized. Three places needed more than a reading. The projection of the proof of Lemma 6.10 does not lie below the two given projections as we read it, and the lemma is proved by another construction, without the hypothesis that $T$ is Fredholm (§VI.4). The isomorphism $\Phi_E$ of formula (94) does not vary continuously in the topology of $\mathrm{DET}$ where $\dim\operatorname{coker}T$ changes parity, as we read it, so the propagation uses $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}T}\Phi_E$ (§VI.14); the map $h \mapsto \tilde h$ of Remark 6.42 gets the same sign (§VI.26). Proposition 6.28 (1), the sc-smooth contractibility of the neighbourhood, is not established by its proof as we read it; what Theorem 6.35 uses is (1′), the homotopy of two paths with the same end points inside a larger region, and that is proved (§§VI.10, VI.18). Five proofs the text omits are supplied: the orientability of a line bundle over a convex set (§VI.9), the general position of Lemma 6.29 (§VI.11), the "simple computation" of Lemma 6.33 (§VI.16), the covering argument of Theorem 6.37 (§VI.22) and the equivalence of Definitions 6.38 and 6.39 (§VI.24). Not formalized: Theorem 6.43 and the admissible sections of §6.6 (gaps G.54, G.55), Proposition 6.28 (1) (gap G.61), the orientation of the solution set as an abstract manifold, its chart independence and the perturbation paragraph after Theorem 6.41 (gaps G.67–G.69), Remark 6.42 beyond a point (gap G.66), the general Lemma 6.19, several remarks, and the facts on paths recalled on p. 201 (§VI.30).

**Six structural choices.** (1) *Chart points.* $T_xX$ carries no linear structure in the formalization (gaps G.6, G.7, G.13 of Chapter 2), so $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ are made at a *chart point* $(c, z)$ of $x$, with operators $T_zO = Dr(z)E \to K_z = \rho(z)F$ on level $0$, and they are identified between charts by explicit transition maps (§VI.21); the text's $f - s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$ is $f + s$ with $(f + s)(x) = 0$. (2) *Global sections, from bump functions.* The text assumes sc-smooth partitions of unity from §6.2 on, "to simplify the presentation" (p. 203). The formalization assumes sc-smooth bump functions, which partitions of unity give (§V.25), and uses them only to make global sc⁺-sections (Findings, Chapter 6, item 43). (3) *Families on $\mathbb R^n$.* Paths, homotopies and families are sc-smooth maps on $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb R^2$, $\mathbb R^n$ whose conditions are imposed on $[0, 1]$, $[0, 1]^2$, $[0, 1]^n$, and $X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R^n \times X$ with the pull-back $\pi^*P$ of the bundle along the projection (decision D2, as for Proposition 6.2 in §III.49; gap G.65; Findings, Chapter 6, item 102). (4) *The sign $\alpha(T) = (-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}T}$* at both end points of every propagation (§VI.14). (5) *(1′), and orientable neighbourhoods as pairs $V \subseteq U$*, since Proposition 6.28 gives (1′) rather than contractibility (§§VI.10, VI.19). (6) *Dyadic subdivisions* in place of the finite coverings of the proof of Theorem 6.37 (§VI.22). An orientation of a line is a ray (Mathlib's `Module.Ray`); an orientation of a topological line bundle is a choice of rays given near every point by a continuous nowhere-zero section.
