**Proposition 7.5** (V7.25) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5⟧. *Let $Y$ be a finite set of mutually isomorphic objects and $V$ a neighbourhood of $Y$. There is a functor $f$ assigning to every $y \in Y$ a connected open $U(y) \subseteq V$, mutually disjoint, and to every $\psi : y \to y'$ between points of $Y$ an sc-diffeomorphism $f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$, such that the morphisms between points of $\bigcup U(y)$ split into components $\mathbf U(\psi)$ with (1) the natural action of $G_y$ on $U(y)$, (2) $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$, $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y')$ sc-diffeomorphisms, (3) $f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$.* The datum is a structure ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite⟧ (Definition 7.8, V7.26), "decomposes into the connected components" being read as: the $\mathbf U(\psi)$ are open, connected, pairwise disjoint and cover; they are then the components ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.connectedComponentIn_morOn⟧ (pp. 233–236).

**The text's proof** (pp. 234–236) is an induction on $\#Y$. $\#Y = 1$ is Theorem 7.1. For $Y = \{y_1, y_2\}$ it fixes $\gamma_1 : y_1 \to y_2$ with a sheet and $\hat\gamma_1 = t \circ (s|\cdot)^{-1}$, takes a $G_{y_1}$-invariant connected $U(y_1)$ with $\hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$ inside a $G_{y_2}$-invariant $W(y_2)$, puts $U(y_2) = \hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$ and shows it invariant; the other morphisms $y_1 \to y_2$ are $g \circ \gamma_1$, $g \in G_{y_2}$, with components $\Phi_g(\mathbf U(\gamma_1))$, $\Phi_g(\varphi) = \Gamma(g, t\varphi) \circ \varphi$, and the morphisms $y_2 \to y_1$ get the inverse components. For $Y = Y' \cup \{y_{k+1}\}$ it fixes $\delta_j : y_{k+1} \to y_j$, shrinks as in the case of two objects, and adjusts the components of the morphisms of $Y'$ to $(s|\mathbf U'(\gamma))^{-1}(U(y_i))$, showing $t(\mathbf U(\gamma)) = U(y_j)$.

**The formalized proof** (V7.25) is a *star*: everything is transported from one base object, and nothing is shrunk afterwards. *Step 1, transport along a sheet.* Let $R = (U, \Phi, \Gamma)$ be a natural representation at $x$ and $\mathbf S_1, \mathbf S_2$ sheets of morphisms out of $x$ with local inverses $a_i = (s|\mathbf S_i)^{-1}$ and $U \subseteq s(\mathbf S_i)$, $\hat\gamma_i = t \circ a_i$. The images $\hat\gamma_i(U)$ are open and connected ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isOpen_transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isConnected_transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_hat_transportSet⟧, $\hat\gamma_i^{-1}$ is the inverse there ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.back⟧, and the conjugates $\hat\gamma_2 \circ \Phi(g) \circ \hat\gamma_1^{-1}$ are sc-diffeomorphisms compatible with composition ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap_conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap_one⟧. The transported morphisms are $\Theta_g(z) = a_2(\Phi(g)u) \circ \Gamma(g, u) \circ a_1(u)^{-1}$, $u = \hat\gamma_1^{-1}(z)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport⟧, with source $z$ and target $\hat\gamma_2(\Phi(g)u)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.src_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.tgt_transport⟧, equal to $\gamma_2 \circ g \circ \gamma_1^{-1}$, $\gamma_i = a_i(x)$, at the point $\hat\gamma_1(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport_hat_self⟧, sc-smooth by (4) in the sheet form, used twice, and the sc-smoothness of $\iota$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScSmoothOn_transport⟧. *Step 2, the bijection.* A morphism $k$ from $\hat\gamma_1(U)$ to $\hat\gamma_2(U)$ pulls back to the morphism $a_2(\cdot)^{-1} \circ k \circ a_1(\cdot)$ between points of $U$, which is $\Gamma(g, u)$ for a unique $g$ by Theorem 7.1 (3); so $k = \Theta_g(sk)$ for a unique $g$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.existsUnique_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport_injective⟧. *Step 3, a natural representation at $y$.* For $\gamma : x \to y$, $h \mapsto \gamma^{-1}h\gamma$ is an isomorphism $G_y \to G_x$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportConj⟧, and $U(y) = \hat\gamma(U)$, $\Phi_y(h) = \hat\gamma \circ \Phi(\gamma^{-1}h\gamma) \circ \hat\gamma^{-1}$, $\Gamma_y(h, \cdot) = \Theta_{\gamma^{-1}h\gamma}$ is a natural representation at $y$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_U⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_Φ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_Γ⟧, after shrinking $R$ (same $\Phi$, $\Gamma$) into $s$ of a sheet of $\gamma$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.exists_spoke⟧. *Step 4, the star.* Fix one $x$ isomorphic to all of $Y$, morphisms $\gamma_y : x \to y$ with sheets $\mathbf K_y$, and by Hausdorff separation of the finite $Y$ pairwise disjoint open $W_y \ni y$; take $U_0 = \bigcap_y (s(\mathbf K_y) \cap \hat\gamma_y^{-1}(W_y \cap V))$ and a natural representation inside $U_0$ (Theorem 7.1) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.exists_star⟧. Then $U(y) = \hat\gamma_y(U(x)) \subseteq W_y \cap V$ are pairwise disjoint. *Step 5, the functor.* $\psi \mapsto g_\psi = \gamma_{y'}^{-1} \circ \psi \circ \gamma_y \in G_x$ is a bijection from the morphisms $y \to y'$ onto $G_x$ compatible with composition, units and inverses ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_inv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_isotropy⟧; $f(\psi) = \hat\gamma_{y'} \circ \Phi(g_\psi) \circ \hat\gamma_y^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F⟧ is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.isScDiffeoOn_F⟧ and a functor, since $\psi \mapsto g_\psi$ is one and $\Phi$ is a homomorphism ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F_unit⟧. *Step 6, the components.* $\mathbf U(\psi) = \Theta_{g_\psi}(U(y))$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.Θ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.sheet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.mem_sheet⟧ are pairwise disjoint ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.pairwiseDisjoint_sheet⟧ and cover the morphisms between points of $\bigcup U(y)$, by Step 2 ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.morOn_eq⟧; $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms on them, as images of sections ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_src_image_of_section⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_image_of_section⟧, and $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1} = f(\psi)$. *Step 7, (1).* The natural representation of $G_y$ on $U(y)$ is the transported one of Step 3, whose $\Phi_y$ is $f$ on $G_y$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.toNaturalRepFinite⟧; by §VII.9 it agrees near $y$ with every other one. The text instead chooses $U(y)$ invariant under a natural representation of $G_y$ given beforehand. The text's case of two objects already has this form ($U(y_2) = \hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$); the adjustment of the components of $Y'$ in the inductive step has no counterpart. "A neighbourhood $V$ of $Y$" is a neighbourhood of the set ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_of_mem_nhdsSet⟧, reduced to an open one; $Y = \emptyset$ is allowed ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.emptyNaturalRepFinite⟧, and enlarging $V$ keeps a datum ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.mono⟧. "Mutually isomorphic" is used only through one $x$ isomorphic to all of $Y$. Among the possible misprints of the proof (Findings, Chapter 7, item 26): "$\Phi_g$" for $g \in G_{y_1}$ where $t(\varphi) \in U(y_2)$ requires $G_{y_2}$; "$\mathbf U(\gamma_g) := \Psi_g(\mathbf U(\gamma_1))$" for $\Phi_g$; the induction step "let $k \ge 3$", which must start at $k \ge 2$ to reach $\#Y = 3$; "$\varphi = \Gamma(g, s(\varphi)) \circ \psi$" for $\Gamma(g, t(\psi)) \circ \psi$; "$y : \mathbf U(\delta_j) \to U(y_j)$" for $t$; and "$g \in G_{y_i}$" for $G_{y_j}$ on p. 236 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 25, 26).

### VII.11 Proposition 7.6 and Definition 7.9: $|U(x)| = G_x\backslash U(x)$, local uniformizers

**Proposition 7.6** (V7.27) ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_6⟧. *For a natural representation at $x$, $\tau : G_x\backslash U(x) \to |U(x)| = \pi(U(x))$, $G_x \ast y \mapsto |y|$, is a homeomorphism.* $G_x\backslash U(x)$ is the orbit space of the action $g \ast y$ with the quotient topology. **The text's proof**: $\tau$ is well defined and onto; it is injective because a morphism $\varphi : y \to y'$ is $\Gamma(g, y)$ by Theorem 7.1 (3), so $y' = g \ast y$; $|U(x)|$ is open by Proposition 7.1; and $\tau \circ \sigma = \pi|U(x)$ for the open quotient map $\sigma$, so $\tau$ is continuous and open. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* $|y| = |y'|$ iff $y' = g \ast y$ for some $g$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_eq_π_iff_exists_smul⟧. *Step 2.* $\tau$ as a map into $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.orbitQuotientMap⟧ is continuous by the quotient topology and injective by Step 1. *Step 3, open.* The image of an open $Q$ is $\pi(\sigma^{-1}(Q))$, and $\sigma^{-1}(Q)$ is open in the open $U(x)$, so Proposition 7.1 applies; the openness of $\sigma$ is not needed. So $\tau$ is an open embedding into $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_orbitQuotientMap⟧ with range $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_orbitQuotientMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_6_apply_mk⟧. *The second form.* The functor $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ of §VII.8 is fully faithful ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_6_fullyFaithful⟧, and the same argument for the orbit space of the translation groupoid, whose classes are the same orbits, gives an open embedding with range $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_orbitMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_functor_orbitMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_6_orbitMap⟧, with $|U(x)|_{G_x \ltimes U(x)} \cong G_x\backslash U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.translationOrbitHomeomorph⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 27) (pp. 236–237).

**Definition 7.9** (V7.28). A local uniformizer around $x$ is a fully faithful functor $\Psi_x : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$, the inclusion on objects, inducing a homeomorphism of $|U(x)|_{G_x \ltimes U(x)}$ onto the open $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer⟧. "Embedding" is not a separate field: the injectivity on objects and morphisms, which the text notes after the definition, follows from the inclusion on objects and faithfulness ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_obj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_mor⟧; for the uniformizers built from natural representations it is also topological, $\Psi_x$ being an open embedding on objects and on morphisms ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_obj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_functor_mor⟧. "There exists a local uniformizer around every object": every natural representation is one ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.toLocalUniformizer⟧, and one exists inside every open $V \ni x$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.exists_localUniformizer⟧; its orbit map is a homeomorphism onto the open $|U(x)|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.isOpen_image⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.orbitHomeomorph⟧. "$\Psi_x \circ G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$" is read with $:$, and "a a local uniformizer" has a doubled article (possible misprints; Findings, Chapter 7, item 28) (p. 237).

### VII.12 Definition 7.10, the M-polyfold $\mathbf A$, and Proposition 7.7

**Definition 7.10** (V7.29). An ep-subgroupoid is the full subcategory on a set $A$ of objects which is a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.12, §II.10) and saturated ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid⟧. Witnesses: $X$ itself ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_univ⟧, every saturated open set ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_of_isOpen⟧, the saturation of every open set, open by Proposition 7.1 ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_saturation⟧, and every sub-M-polyfold of a trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_trivial⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 40, 105) (p. 237).

**The facts (1)–(4) on $A$** (V7.30). By Part I's Proposition 2.6 (§II.10), $A$ has an M-polyfold structure ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subObjPolyfold⟧ with (1) the inclusion sc-smooth and a homeomorphism onto its image ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subObj⟧ and (2) $i^{-1} \circ r$ sc-smooth for every sc-smooth retraction $r$ onto $A \cap V$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subObj⟧. The tangent facts (3), (4) are not restated, since $T_aA$ and $T_aX$ carry no linear structure here (gap G.7); in a chart they are Part I's ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_21_3⟧, and nothing below uses them (Findings, Chapter 7, item 40) (pp. 237–238).

**$\mathbf A$ is a sub-M-polyfold** (V7.31). The text takes, for $\varphi \in \mathbf A$ with $a = s(\varphi)$, a sheet $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(a)$ and a retraction $r$ of $U(a)$ onto $U(a) \cap A$, and shows that $\mathbf r = (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ r \circ s$ retracts $\mathbf U(\varphi)$ onto $\mathbf U(\varphi) \cap \mathbf A$. *Step 1, saturation.* For saturated $A$, $t(\varphi) \in A$ iff $s(\varphi) \in A$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.src_mem_of_tgt_mem_of_isSaturated⟧, so $\mathbf A = s^{-1}(A) = t^{-1}(A)$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_tgt⟧. *Step 2, a more general statement.* The preimage of a sub-M-polyfold under a local sc-diffeomorphism is one: the retraction is pulled back along a sheet, after shrinking $U(a)$ to $(V \cap V_0) \cap r^{-1}(V \cap V_0)$ so that $r$ maps it into itself ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · isSubMPolyfold_preimage_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_tgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_morOn⟧. So $\mathbf A$ is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subMorPolyfold⟧ with facts (1), (2) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subMor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subMor⟧; its paracompactness, which the project's M-polyfolds need, is that of a subspace of a metrizable space. The text's "$s(\mathbf r(\psi)) = r(s(\psi)) \in A$ and $t(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in U(a)$" is not used: the second claim does not hold in general as we read it, $t(\mathbf r(\psi))$ lying near $t(\varphi)$ rather than near $a$, and $s(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in A$ with saturation gives $t(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in A$ (possible misprint or extraction artefact for $s(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in U(a)$; Findings, Chapter 7, item 41) (p. 238).

**Proposition 7.7** (V7.32) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_7⟧. *For a saturated sub-M-polyfold $A$, the full subcategory on $A$ is an ep-groupoid; $A$ and $\mathbf A$ are sub-M-polyfolds, and all structure maps are the restrictions of those of $X$.* The text checks the conditions of Definition 7.3 in a few lines; the formalization supplies the unstated step that *a map into a sub-M-polyfold which is sc-smooth into the ambient M-polyfold is sc-smooth into the sub-M-polyfold*: near a point it is $(i^{-1} \circ r) \circ i \circ f$, by fact (2) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · isScSmoothOn_subPolyfold_of_val⟧. *(1).* A sheet of $s$ maps $\mathbf U(\varphi) \cap \mathbf A$ onto $U(a) \cap A$; with the unstated step, $s$ and $t$ restrict to local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_tgt⟧. *(2).* $u$ and $\iota$ are restrictions ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_inv⟧. *(3).* The text uses a $U(a)$ with the natural $G_a$-action and $t$ proper over $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_XU(a))$ and notes that $U(a) \cap A$ is invariant; the invariance is not used, and any $V(a)$ of Definition 7.3 (3) works with $V(a) \cap A$: a sequence with sources in $\mathrm{cl}_A(V(a) \cap A) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XV(a)$ and convergent targets in $A$ has a subsequence converging in $\mathbf X$ (§VII.2), whose source lies in $A$ by saturation and in $\mathrm{cl}_A(V(a) \cap A)$ since this set is closed in $A$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_fullSub⟧. *(4), literally.* The inclusion $\mathbf A\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf A \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is sc-smooth between the fibred products of Proposition 2.15, by the unstated step applied twice, and $m$ of $A$ is $m$ of $X$ composed with it ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.fullSub_comp_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_fullSub⟧. So the full subcategory is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid⟧ whose structure maps are the restrictions ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_src_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_comp_val⟧, and the inclusion is a full and faithful ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_full⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_faithful⟧, which the text does not state. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the paracompactness of $A$ and $\mathbf A$ is proved (Findings, Chapter 7, item 42) (pp. 238–239).

### VII.13 Definition 7.11, Lemmas 7.2 and 7.3

**Definition 7.11** (V7.33). $X$ is *effective* if for every $x$, every $g \in G_x \setminus \{1_x\}$ and every open neighbourhood $\mathbf U(g)$ there is $\psi \in \mathbf U(g)$ with $s(\psi) \ne t(\psi)$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsEffective⟧; $x$ is *regular* if $G_x = \{1_x\}$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.IsRegular⟧, and $X_{reg}$ is the set of regular objects ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.regularSet⟧. "If $s(\varphi)$ is regular, so is $t(\varphi)$": conjugation with $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of isotropy groups (§VII.6) ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.isRegular_tgt_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isRegular_tgt_of_isRegular_src⟧, so $X_{reg}$ is saturated ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_regularSet⟧. The definition is satisfiable non-vacuously, by $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $\mathbb R$ by reflection (§VII.30) ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isEffective_reflection_nonvacuous⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 50, 101) (p. 239).

**Lemma 7.2** (V7.34) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2⟧. *$X_{reg}$ is open.* For regular $x$ and a natural representation at $x$, every morphism $\varphi : a \to b$ between points of $U(x)$ is $\Gamma(1_x, a)$ by Theorem 7.1 (3), and $\Gamma(1_x, a) = 1_a$ (§VII.8); so $b = a$, $\varphi = 1_a$, and $G_a$ is trivial. The formalization proves the stronger statement that $U(x) \subseteq X_{reg}$ for *every* natural representation at a regular $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.subset_regularSet⟧. *Hidden hypothesis:* $\Gamma(1, a) = 1_a$, which needs $U(x)$ connected. "Examples show that the regular set can be empty" is the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action (§VII.30) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 51) (p. 239).

**Lemma 7.3** (V7.35) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3⟧. *Equivalent: (1) $X$ is effective; (2) every open $V(x)$ contains a natural representation with $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x))$ injective.* Injectivity is read as "$\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on $U$ only for $g = 1$" ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.injective_Φ_iff⟧, the triviality of the kernel of $G_x \to \mathrm{Perm}(U)$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_kerΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff_injective⟧. **The text's proof.** (1) ⇒ (2) by contradiction: if $\Phi(h) = 1$ with $h \ne 1$, effectiveness gives $\varphi_k \to h$ with $s(\varphi_k) \ne t(\varphi_k)$; $\varphi_k = \Gamma(h_k, s\varphi_k)$ with $h_k \ne h$, after a subsequence $h_k = g$, and in the limit $h = \Gamma(g, x) = g$. (2) ⇒ (1): $\Phi(g) \ne 1$ gives $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$, and $\Gamma(g, a)$ has $s \ne t$; "by taking smaller and smaller neighborhoods $U(x)$ and adapting the corresponding restrictions of $\Gamma$" one finds such morphisms converging to $g$. **The formalized proof.** *(1) ⇒ (2), for every natural representation, without sequences* ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.IsEffective.eq_one⟧. If $\Phi(h) = 1$ on $U$, the sheet $\Gamma(h, U)$ is an open neighbourhood of $h$ on which $s = t$, since $t(\Gamma(h, y)) = \Phi(h)(y) = y$; effectiveness forces $h = 1$. So effectiveness is the injectivity of every natural representation ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_forall_naturalRep⟧, and natural representations exist inside every $V(x)$ (§VII.9). *(2) ⇒ (1).* Fix one natural representation $R_0 = (U_0, \Phi_0, \Gamma_0)$, $g \ne 1$ and an open $\mathbf U(g)$. *Step 1.* Apply (2) once, to $V = \{y \in U_0 \mid \Gamma_0(g, y) \in \mathbf U(g)\}$, open and containing $x$. *Step 2.* The natural representation $R$ that (2) gives inside $V$ has $\Phi(g) \ne 1$, so some $a \in U$ has $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$. *Step 3.* $R$ need not be a restriction of $R_0$, as we read "adapting the corresponding restrictions"; it agrees with $R_0$ on the component of $x$ in $U \cap U_0 = U$, i.e. on $U$ (§VII.9) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn_of_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn_of_subset⟧. *Step 4.* So $\Gamma_0(g, a) = \Gamma(g, a) \in \mathbf U(g)$ has source $a$ and target $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$. One application of (2) suffices (Findings, Chapter 7, item 52) (pp. 239–240).

### VII.14 Proposition 7.8

**Proposition 7.8** (V7.36) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_8⟧. *If $X$ is effective, $X_{reg}$ is open and dense.* **The text's proof**: in a $U(x_0)$ take $x$ with $\#G_x$ minimal; if $\#G_x > 1$, Lemma 7.3 gives $U(x) \subseteq U(x_0)$ with $\Phi$ injective and, for $g \ne 1$, a point $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$; $G_a$ is isomorphic to $H = \{h \in G_x \mid \Phi(h)(a) = a\}$, so $\#G_x \le \#G_a = \#H \le \#G_x$, $H = G_x$, a contradiction. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* For a natural representation at $x$ and $a \in U$, $h \mapsto \Gamma(h, a)$ is an isomorphism from the stabilizer of $a$ onto $G_a$, by Theorem 7.1 (3) and the functoriality of $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy⟧. *Step 2.* Given a nonempty open $O$, take $x \in O$ minimizing $\#G_x$ over $O$ itself, so the text's $U(x_0)$ is not needed. *Step 3.* If $G_x \ne 1$, take a natural representation inside $O$ (§VII.9), injective by Lemma 7.3, $g \ne 1$ and $a \in U$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$; then $\#G_a = \#\mathrm{Stab}(a) < \#G_x$, contradicting minimality. So $O$ meets $X_{reg}$; openness is Lemma 7.2. Only $\#G_a < \#G_x$ is used. *The converse* holds too, and is not in the text ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_of_dense_regularSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_dense_regularSet⟧: if $X_{reg}$ is dense and $g \ne 1$, a regular $a$ near $x$ with $\Gamma(g, a)$ in a given $\mathbf U(g)$ has $\Gamma(g, a) \ne 1_a = \Gamma(1, a)$, so $s \ne t$ there (Findings, Chapter 7, item 53) (pp. 240–241).

### VII.15 The subgroups $T_x$, and Definition 7.12

**$T_x$** (V7.37). $g \in G_x$ *acts trivially* if $\Phi(g) = 1$ for some natural representation ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ActsTrivially⟧, and $T_x$ is the set of such $g$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivialSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.one_mem_trivialSet⟧. The text: since $G_x$ is finite, $U(x)$ can be chosen so small that the kernel of $\Phi$ is $T_x$, a normal subgroup as a kernel. Since sc-smooth maps are not analytic, $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ does not give $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on a connected $U(x)$, so the kernel can depend on $U(x)$; the text's "small" is made precise in three statements. *Step 1, for every representation.* $g \in T_x$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$, for any given natural representation (§VII.9, Step 4) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.actsTrivially_iff⟧. *Step 2, intrinsically.* $g \in T_x$ iff $s = t$ on a neighbourhood of $g$ in $\mathbf X$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_iff_eventually⟧: one direction is the sheet $\Gamma(g, U)$; for the other, a continuous section of $s$ through $g$ along which $s = t$ near $x$ gives $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_of_section⟧. *Step 3, small neighbourhoods.* For one $R_0$, the common fixed set in $U_0$ of the finitely many elements of $T_x$ is a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$, and $\ker\Phi = T_x$ for *every* natural representation inside $N$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_mem_nhds_trivialSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_trivialSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_kerΦ_eq⟧. *Step 4.* So $T_x$ is a kernel, a normal subgroup ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSubgroup⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_normal⟧, its own normal closure ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.normalClosure_trivialSet⟧, and by Step 2 Definition 7.11 says exactly $T_x = \{1_x\}$ for all $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot⟧. *At nearby points.* For $g \in \ker\Phi$, $\Gamma(g, y) \in T_y$ for $y \in U$, which the proof of Proposition 7.9 uses ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_trivialSet_of_val_eq_Γ⟧. *Along a morphism, not stated in the text.* For $\varphi : x \to y$ and $g \in T_x$, $z \mapsto \theta(z) \circ \Gamma(g, s\theta(z)) \circ \theta(z)^{-1}$, $\theta = (t|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$, is a continuous section of $s$ through $\varphi g \varphi^{-1}$ — by (4) in the sheet form, twice — along which $s = t$ near $y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_conj_section⟧; by Step 2, $\varphi g\varphi^{-1} \in T_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet_iff⟧, and $\varphi T_x\varphi^{-1} = T_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.map_isotropyConj_trivialSubgroup⟧. This is what the descent of the composition to $\mathbf X^R$ needs. "$\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x)$" lacks a parenthesis (possible misprint or extraction artefact). Witnesses: $T_x = 1$ for the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_trivial⟧ and the reflection, $T_x = G_x \cong \mathbb Z/3$ for the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action (§VII.30) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 54) (p. 241).

**Definition 7.12** (V7.38). $\mathbf X^T = \bigcup_x T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart⟧; $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $s(\varphi) = s(\varphi') = x$ and $\varphi = \varphi' \circ g$ with $g \in T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel⟧; $\mathbf X^R$ is the set of classes ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ReducedMor⟧. *Step 1, $\mathbf X^T$ intrinsically.* By §VII.15 Step 2, $\mathbf X^T$ is the interior of $\{\varphi \mid s\varphi = t\varphi\}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_interior⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.val_mem_nonEffectivePart_iff⟧, open ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpen_nonEffectivePart⟧ and closed under units, inverses, composition and conjugation ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.unit_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.inv_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.comp_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.conj_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧. So $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $\varphi = \varphi' \circ k$ with $k \in \mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff⟧, a form without dependent types. *Step 2, an equivalence relation,* because $T_x$ is a subgroup ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_refl⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedSetoid⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedMor_eq_quotient⟧. *Step 3, the left form.* By the conjugation $\varphi T_x\varphi^{-1} = T_y$, $\varphi \sim \psi$ iff $\varphi = k \circ \psi$ with $k \in T_{t\psi}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.exists_comp_left⟧; the relation respects $s$, $t$, $\iota$ and composition on both sides ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.src_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.tgt_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.inv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.comp_right⟧. "The subset $\mathbf X^R$ of reduced morphisms" is a quotient, as the next sentence of the text says (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 55) (p. 241).

### VII.16 Proposition 7.9: the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$

**Proposition 7.9** (V7.39) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_9⟧. *$\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure.* **The text's proof**: $\mathbf X^R$ carries the quotient topology; on a sheet $s : U(\varphi_0) \to U(s\varphi_0)$ the projection $\pi'$ is continuous and injective; its image $U([\varphi_0])$ is open, by the map $\delta(\psi') = \psi' \circ \Gamma(g, s\psi')$ near an equivalent $\psi$, with $U(s\psi)$ chosen with $\ker\Phi = T_{s\psi}$; the same argument shows $\Psi_{\varphi_0} : U(\varphi_0) \to U([\varphi_0])$ open; and the transitions are, near $\varphi$ with $\psi = \varphi \circ g$, the sc-smooth $\delta$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the topology.* The projection $\pi^R : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedπ_eq_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedπ⟧ is a quotient map ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isQuotientMap_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.continuous_reducedπ⟧. *Step 2, $\pi^R$ is open* ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ⟧. The text's $\delta$ composes on the right with a section of $s$; its continuity holds by (4) applied to inverses. The left form is used instead: for $\varphi \sim \psi$, $\varphi = \Gamma(g, t\psi) \circ \psi$ near $\psi$ with $g \in T_{t\psi}$ and a natural representation with $\ker\Phi = T_{t\psi}$ (§VII.15); $\delta(\psi') = \Gamma(g, t\psi') \circ \psi'$ is sc-smooth by (4) in the sheet form ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothOn_comp_Γ_tgt⟧ and $\psi' \sim \delta(\psi')$ since $\Gamma(g, t\psi') \in T_{t\psi'}$. So the saturation of an open set is open. *Step 3, sheets.* On every sheet $s : \mathbf W \to V$, $\pi^R$ is injective — equivalent morphisms have the same source — and hence an open embedding ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.injOn_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ_image_Γ⟧; "small" sheets are not needed. *Step 4, charts.* For a chart $\psi$ of $\mathbf X$ with domain in a sheet $\mathbf W$, $\sigma = (s|\mathbf W)^{-1}$, the chart of $\mathbf X^R$ is $[\varphi'] \mapsto \psi(\sigma(s[\varphi']))$ on $\pi^R(\mathrm{dom}\,\psi)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart⟧; every point lies in one ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.exists_chart_sheet⟧. *Step 5, transitions.* On an overlap, an element of the second sheet equivalent to $\varphi'$ has the source $s(\varphi')$, so the text's $\delta$ equals $\sigma_2 \circ s$ and the transition is $\psi_2 \circ \sigma_2 \circ s \circ \psi_1^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart_transition⟧, sc-smooth; what needs the text's argument is that the overlap is open, i.e. Step 2 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.overlap_reducedChart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart_compatible⟧. The charts form an atlas ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedCharts⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedAtlas⟧, all without hypotheses. *Step 6, Hausdorff and paracompact.* An M-polyfold is a Hausdorff paracompact space (Definition 2.8). The proof gives neither as we read it, and $\mathbf X^R$ need not be Hausdorff (a splicing example, not formalized); so the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$ is built under the hypotheses that $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff and paracompact ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isChart_reducedChart⟧, and then $\pi^R$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, with inverse $\sigma \circ s$ on $\pi^R(\mathbf W)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedπ⟧ (gap G.71). *The hypotheses are satisfiable.* For effective $X$, $\sim$ is equality ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff_eq_of_isEffective⟧, $\pi^R$ a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedHomeomorph⟧, and $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff, paracompact and regular ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t3Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧; this covers the trivial ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_trivial⟧. Paracompactness also follows from regularity of $\mathbf X^R$ when $\mathbf X$ is second countable ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_t3⟧; Hausdorffness alone with $\mathbf X$ second countable is not shown to suffice, a second countable, locally metrizable Hausdorff space need not be regular. Four possible misprints of the proof: "$\psi' = (s|U(\psi))^{-1}(s(\psi))$" for $s(\psi')$, "$U(\varphi) \subset \Psi_{\varphi_0}(U([\varphi_0]) \cap U([\psi_0]))$" for $\Psi_{\varphi_0}^{-1}$, "$T_x$ agrees with the kernel of the $G_{s(\varphi)}$-action" for $T_{s(\varphi)}$, and a garbled sentence on the smoothness of the source and target maps (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 57, 60, 111) (pp. 242–243).

### VII.17 The reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, Proposition 7.10, Definition 7.13

**$X_R$** (V7.40). Objects $X$, morphisms $\mathbf X^R$, $s([\varphi]) = s(\varphi)$, $t([\varphi]) = t(\varphi)$, with unit, inverse and composition descended by §VII.15 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedTgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedInv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedComp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedComp_π⟧, $s$ and $t$ onto ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedTgt⟧, a groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedGroupoidStr⟧; the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value, as in §VII.1 (p. 243).

**Proposition 7.10** (V7.40) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_10⟧. *Under the hypotheses of §VII.16, $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid, and it is effective.* *(1).* For a sheet $\mathbf W$ of Definition 7.4, $s, t : \pi^R(\mathbf W) \to X$ are $s \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$ and $t \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$, the text's $s(\Psi_\varphi(\varphi')) = s(\varphi')$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedTgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedTgt⟧. *(2).* $u = \pi^R \circ u_X$ and $\iota = \pi^R \circ \iota_X \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$ on $\pi^R(\mathbf W)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedInv⟧. *(3), "proved similarly".* For the same $V(x)$, $t \circ \pi^R = t_X$ on $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}V(x))$, with $\pi^R$ a continuous surjection onto the corresponding set of $\mathbf X^R$; a map whose composite with a continuous surjection is proper is proper (Mathlib) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_reduced⟧. *(4), "reduced by our local charts",* in the sheet form: for an sc-diffeomorphism $s : \mathbf W' \to V'$ of $\mathbf X^R$ with inverse $\sigma'$, $\kappa = \sigma_2 \circ s \circ \sigma'$ is the inverse of $s$ on an open set of $\mathbf X$ — a step the text leaves implicit — and $m(\sigma'(t\psi), \psi) = \pi^R(m(\kappa(t\psi), \psi))$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_reduced⟧. So $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid⟧ and $X \to X_R$ an ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionFunctor⟧. *Effective.* The text's point $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$ is replaced by the intrinsic form of $T_x$: if $s = t$ near $[g]$ in $\mathbf X^R$, then $s = t$ near $g$ in $\mathbf X$, $\pi^R$ being continuous, so $g \in T_x$ and $[g] = [1_x]$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid⟧. For effective $X$, $X_R \cong X$ in $\mathcal{EP}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionInv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionIso⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 58, 60) (p. 244).
